<span id="paper-recommendation-aigq-4359f5f2" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-85620789beeec609">Why treat suggested queries as a set rather than independent strings?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aaigq">AIGQ: An End-to-End Hybrid Generative Architecture for E-commerce Query Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group / Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A group defines exploration coverage. Per-item plausibility can yield repetitive outputs; group rewards evaluate coverage and engagement, subject to reward quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Five paraphrases add less than options covering director, mood, and duration.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.19710">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.19710-aigq/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-85620789beeec609">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:aigq" data-paper-title="AIGQ: An End-to-End Hybrid Generative Architecture for E-commerce Query Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-49d1587cf0ff9fec">Why keep Direct and Reasoning query paths?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aaigq">AIGQ: An End-to-End Hybrid Generative Architecture for E-commerce Query Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group / Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Easy intent benefits from low latency and complex intent from deeper inference. IL-GRPO aligns query groups, while hybrid offline/online serving reduces request cost. Local proxies do not reproduce CTR rewards or the live stack.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Directly complete a brand, but reason about recipient and use for vague gifts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.19710">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.19710-aigq/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-49d1587cf0ff9fec">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:aigq" data-paper-title="AIGQ: An End-to-End Hybrid Generative Architecture for E-commerce Query Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-138f5c947c2e69f0">What update risk does KL control beyond CTR reward?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aaigq">AIGQ: An End-to-End Hybrid Generative Architecture for E-commerce Query Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group / Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reference KL penalizes drifting into narrow or reward-hacking queries. It balances feedback against prior behavior without guaranteeing unbiased rewards or independent quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Avoid making every suggestion clickbait just because clicks rise temporarily.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.19710">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.19710-aigq/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-138f5c947c2e69f0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:aigq" data-paper-title="AIGQ: An End-to-End Hybrid Generative Architecture for E-commerce Query Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-83c770e041a1cce0">Does MovieLens validate live IL-GRPO and latency?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aaigq">AIGQ: An End-to-End Hybrid Generative Architecture for E-commerce Query Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group / Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Same candidates/seeds and validation-tuned proxy weights test ranking mechanisms only, without real query CTR or hybrid serving. Account separately for ranking, policy training, and measured latency.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Movie NDCG gains do not establish millisecond query latency or online RL.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.19710">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.19710-aigq/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-83c770e041a1cce0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:angle" data-paper-title="One-Step Retrieval Framework for Real-Time Sponsored Search Ads Using Hierarchical Text Representations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-angle-c3d4b151" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-b36cbacb54bf77e0">Why is intent × summary an ad hierarchy rather than an ordinary ID?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aangle">One-Step Retrieval Framework for Real-Time Sponsored Search Ads Using Hierarchical Text Representations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Intent groups needs and summary refines meaning, so paths share information. Joint objectives learn predictive and discriminative IDs, but codes still need real eligible ad mapping.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Generate travel preparation then portable storage, not an unrelated flat ID.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.18296">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.18296-angle/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b36cbacb54bf77e0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:angle" data-paper-title="One-Step Retrieval Framework for Real-Time Sponsored Search Ads Using Hierarchical Text Representations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c4c49ab8f4fbbd8c">Why dynamically constrain decoding despite hierarchical ad IDs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aangle">One-Step Retrieval Framework for Real-Time Sponsored Search Ads Using Hierarchical Text Representations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Hierarchy organizes ads but not request-specific eligibility. Constrained beams exclude invalid paths during search, while generation/discrimination/ranking learn relevance. Postfiltering can waste beams.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Block an unavailable ad path before it consumes the candidate budget.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.18296">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.18296-angle/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c4c49ab8f4fbbd8c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:angle" data-paper-title="One-Step Retrieval Framework for Real-Time Sponsored Search Ads Using Hierarchical Text Representations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-4d08c0ebac8b3d6b">How does adding discrimination differ from beam selection by likelihood alone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aangle">One-Step Retrieval Framework for Real-Time Sponsored Search Ads Using Hierarchical Text Representations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Likelihood expresses contextual path probability; discrimination measures target specificity and ranking links utility. Tune their trade-off on validation; neither guarantees all metrics improve.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A popular summary can lose to a more suitable niche path, unless discrimination is overweighted.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.18296">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.18296-angle/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4d08c0ebac8b3d6b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:angle" data-paper-title="One-Step Retrieval Framework for Real-Time Sponsored Search Ads Using Hierarchical Text Representations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-2c29b4cbdc3fb8c6">Should ANGLE filter illegal beams after generation or at every expansion?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aangle">One-Step Retrieval Framework for Real-Time Sponsored Search Ads Using Hierarchical Text Representations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Apply request-specific legality at every step. Global vocabulary is not current eligibility. Select fusion coefficients on validation only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Mask a region-ineligible prefix immediately rather than generate ten ads and reject nine.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.18296">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.18296-angle/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2c29b4cbdc3fb8c6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:barge" data-paper-title="Bridging the Structural Gap: Adapting Autoregressive Generation for Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-barge-1cfb2666" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-321f5c75e23f3457">Why do multiple SID tokens for one BARGE item require explicit item context?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Abarge">Bridging the Structural Gap: Adapting Autoregressive Generation for Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>They are decompositions of the same item, but ordinary sequence attention may treat them as independent events. ICA aggregates within-item context and gates it back into each token, joining whole-item meaning to local detail. This addresses representation structure, not the separate task of learning preferences across items.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A book&#x27;s topic, subcategory, and collision code describe one book, not three successive reads.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.21028">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.21028-barge/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-321f5c75e23f3457">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:barge" data-paper-title="Bridging the Structural Gap: Adapting Autoregressive Generation for Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1164e6c8c83dd97c">Why does BARGE both restore item boundaries and rerank accumulated semantic paths?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Abarge">Bridging the Structural Gap: Adapting Autoregressive Generation for Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Ordinary sequence attention can treat the multiple SID codes of one item as separate events; ICA aggregates within-item context and gates it back into each code. HPR evaluates the accumulated generated path to limit propagation of early beam mistakes, while complementary quantization gives alternate decomposition views. These address boundaries, search errors, and diversity respectively.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Province, city, and street are one address, not three purchases. If the coarse province is wrong, refining the street cannot fix it, so check the path at every level.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.21028">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.21028-barge/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1164e6c8c83dd97c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:barge" data-paper-title="Bridging the Structural Gap: Adapting Autoregressive Generation for Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-63bc94c75b23ca7b">How do BARGE&#x27;s two complementary decoding paths differ from widening a single beam?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Abarge">Bridging the Structural Gap: Adapting Autoregressive Generation for Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A wider beam searches more paths within one encoding structure. Two orthogonal subspaces construct different representations and quantizations, so one early bias need not dominate both. HPR then scores cumulative paths. Extra paths add training and merge costs, and output count alone does not prove complementarity or independence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A wider beam may still explore a mistaken coarse code, while a second subspace can recover a missed book if it preserves different semantic cues.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.21028">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.21028-barge/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-63bc94c75b23ca7b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:barge" data-paper-title="Bridging the Structural Gap: Adapting Autoregressive Generation for Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-263c5784a60fb5af">Why does BARGE&#x27;s HPR compare the accumulated path vector instead of only the latest code?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Abarge">Bridging the Structural Gap: Adapting Autoregressive Generation for Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The cumulative sum includes every choice from coarse to fine and reveals whether the full semantic path fits the user. During inference combine generation log-probability with reranking; during training use contrastive comparisons over cumulative paths. DPD separately constrains projection orthogonality; it is not the same loss or proof of full independence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An entry-level code makes sense on its own, but the path has already entered home goods while the user wants a camera. Only the accumulated path exposes the mismatch.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.21028">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.21028-barge/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-263c5784a60fb5af">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:climber-pilot" data-paper-title="Climber-Pilot: A Non-Myopic Generative Recommendation Model Towards Better Instruction-Following" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-climber-pilot-a97c0a4c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-96e822a73ea4b59e">Why can Climber-Pilot predict multiple future items in training but serve in one step?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aclimber-pilot">Climber-Pilot: A Non-Myopic Generative Recommendation Model Towards Better Instruction-Following</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NetEase Cloud Music</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Offset targets inject long-horizon consumption structure into a shared current state, and time weights differentiate offsets. Serving uses that learned model directly without simulating the future or seeing those targets.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Train the current state to predict the upcoming camera, lens, and bag; score today&#x27;s candidates without access to those true future events.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.13581">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.13581-climber-pilot/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-96e822a73ea4b59e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:climber-pilot" data-paper-title="Climber-Pilot: A Non-Myopic Generative Recommendation Model Towards Better Instruction-Following" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-93eb6feb5d5e3d8d">How does Climber-Pilot account for farther-future consumption without serving a full rollout?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aclimber-pilot">Climber-Pilot: A Non-Myopic Generative Recommendation Model Towards Better Instruction-Following</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NetEase Cloud Music</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Time-aware multi-item prediction trains the current state on several future targets, embedding longer-horizon structure in the parameters. Serving can still generate one result; condition-guided attention adds category and business constraints without extra rollout steps. True future items belong only to training supervision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Training can learn that camera interest extends to accessories. Serving cannot read a user&#x27;s future purchase to recommend now.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.13581">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.13581-climber-pilot/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-93eb6feb5d5e3d8d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:climber-pilot" data-paper-title="Climber-Pilot: A Non-Myopic Generative Recommendation Model Towards Better Instruction-Following" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-92cad7296cf78cda">At what stage do constraints act in Climber-Pilot&#x27;s conditional sparse attention versus post-decoding filtering?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aclimber-pilot">Climber-Pilot: A Non-Myopic Generative Recommendation Model Towards Better Instruction-Following</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NetEase Cloud Music</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>An internal attention mask changes which evidence forms the representation; post-filtering only removes generated results and cannot recover legal options that generation omitted. Internal masks must match business rules and do not eliminate the need for legality checks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A category mask can guide candidate formation. Removing all invalid candidates after generation can leave an empty list and cannot recover spent generation budget.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.13581">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.13581-climber-pilot/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-92cad7296cf78cda">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:climber-pilot" data-paper-title="Climber-Pilot: A Non-Myopic Generative Recommendation Model Towards Better Instruction-Following" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c107ef20782d3df8">How should TAMIP time weights interact with valid-target masks in the multi-future loss?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aclimber-pilot">Climber-Pilot: A Non-Myopic Generative Recommendation Model Towards Better Instruction-Following</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NetEase Cloud Music</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Offset k needs a real target and its specified weight `w_k`; padding at the tail of short sequences is not positive supervision. Offsets can share a current state whose inputs stop at the cutoff. Time-weighted losses and conditional attention masks affect different tensors.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>With two future events, compute two loss terms. A third empty slot creates no fake target, and heavier weighting does not let a future event enter history.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.13581">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.13581-climber-pilot/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c107ef20782d3df8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cobra" data-paper-title="Sparse Meets Dense: Unified Generative Recommendations with Cascaded Sparse-Dense Representations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-cobra-75daff60" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-fe2b493774ecc359">Why generate COBRA&#x27;s sparse code and dense vector in separate stages?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acobra">Sparse Meets Dense: Unified Generative Recommendations with Cascaded Sparse-Dense Representations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Baidu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A beam selects semantic regions by discrete code, then conditioned nearest-neighbor search preserves fine differences within each region and offsets quantization loss. Dense precision cannot recover items outside every selected region.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Locate science fiction first, then distinguish hard and action science fiction. Fine ranking within family comedy will not find a science-fiction target.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.02453">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2503.02453-cobra/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fe2b493774ecc359">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cobra" data-paper-title="Sparse Meets Dense: Unified Generative Recommendations with Cascaded Sparse-Dense Representations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-fc61d6dcbcc97925">Why does COBRA generate a dense vector conditioned on an already generated sparse SID?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acobra">Sparse Meets Dense: Unified Generative Recommendations with Cascaded Sparse-Dense Representations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Baidu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Quantization retains coarse structure but loses within-code details. The discrete path narrows search; user context and that path generate a dense query to distinguish items sharing a coarse code. Joint objectives align stages, but reranking cannot guarantee recovery of paths eliminated by the beam.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>After choosing athletic shoes, a dense query can distinguish trail from road shoes. It cannot recover them if the beam picked appliances.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.02453">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2503.02453-cobra/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fc61d6dcbcc97925">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cobra" data-paper-title="Sparse Meets Dense: Unified Generative Recommendations with Cascaded Sparse-Dense Representations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a4f74f5dbf88f5b3">What does COBRA borrow from continuous two-tower retrieval and pure SID generation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acobra">Sparse Meets Dense: Unified Generative Recommendations with Cascaded Sparse-Dense Representations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Baidu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Continuous towers suit ANN but often compress a user into few vectors; SID generation nominates hierarchical regions at the cost of quantization errors. COBRA uses codes for multi-region nomination and conditioned vectors for within-region detail, adding modules and calibration. Sparse-only ablation and comparison with DIN answer different questions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A beam can nominate photography and baking separately and refine both, instead of averaging interests in one vector, but both score levels need maintenance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.02453">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2503.02453-cobra/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a4f74f5dbf88f5b3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cobra" data-paper-title="Sparse Meets Dense: Unified Generative Recommendations with Cascaded Sparse-Dense Representations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-889c431918417b06">Why combine COBRA beam scores and conditioned-vector dot products at inference?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acobra">Sparse Meets Dense: Unified Generative Recommendations with Cascaded Sparse-Dense Representations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Baidu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Dot products express item fit conditional on a code; beam scores preserve each path&#x27;s prior plausibility. Combine on compatible scales and choose coefficients on validation. The dense training loss should actually update conditioned vectors, not be replaced by a fixed score mix.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A high local dot product under an unlikely code should not automatically beat a slightly lower score under a likely code.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.02453">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2503.02453-cobra/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-889c431918417b06">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cq-sid" data-paper-title="Efficient Generative Retrieval for E-commerce Search with Semantic Cluster IDs and Expert-Guided RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-cq-sid-a55bb5d1" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-7bbd4888f1acf964">Why use a category first and within-category residuals afterward in CQ-SID?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acq-sid">Efficient Generative Retrieval for E-commerce Search with Semantic Cluster IDs and Expert-Guided RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Taobao &amp; Tmall Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Categories give controllable semantic boundaries; later codes distinguish details inside them. This aligns decoding with catalog constraints but may block items under a wrong category or separate cross-category neighbors.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Choose camera first, then distinguish mirrorless from action cameras. A product misfiled under phone accessories follows the wrong path.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.14434">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.14434-cq-sid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7bbd4888f1acf964">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cq-sid" data-paper-title="Efficient Generative Retrieval for E-commerce Search with Semantic Cluster IDs and Expert-Guided RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b4f87d7ed4915a2b">What does CQ-SID gain and lose by fixing the first code to the item category?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acq-sid">Efficient Generative Retrieval for E-commerce Search with Semantic Cluster IDs and Expert-Guided RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Taobao &amp; Tmall Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The category organizes coarse search and business constraints; residual codes encode within-category detail. Wrong categories can make candidates unreachable, and cross-category substitutes may be split. Expert-guided reward balances clicks, purchases, and constraints; taxonomy alone does not ensure relevance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Generate a shoe code before styles, but a multifunctional product wrongly classified as luggage may never appear in a shoe search.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.14434">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.14434-cq-sid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b4f87d7ed4915a2b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cq-sid" data-paper-title="Efficient Generative Retrieval for E-commerce Search with Semantic Cluster IDs and Expert-Guided RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-fc84f38467d8d233">Where does CQ-SID&#x27;s category constraint differ from a freely learned RQ first code?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acq-sid">Efficient Generative Retrieval for E-commerce Search with Semantic Cluster IDs and Expert-Guided RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Taobao &amp; Tmall Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Free quantization groups coarse codes by representation distance. CQ-SID fixes alignment with taxonomy in training and decoding, reducing semantic drift but depending on catalog quality. Expert-Guided RL separately aligns feedback; clear categories do not ensure higher recall.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A photography book and tutorial video may share a free prefix but split under a fixed catalog taxonomy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.14434">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.14434-cq-sid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fc84f38467d8d233">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cq-sid" data-paper-title="Efficient Generative Retrieval for E-commerce Search with Semantic Cluster IDs and Expert-Guided RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-11cee61cb6af22a3">Within what scope should CQ-SID normalize grouped advantages?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acq-sid">Efficient Generative Retrieval for E-commerce Search with Semantic Cluster IDs and Expert-Guided RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Taobao &amp; Tmall Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Compute reward mean and standard deviation among rollouts for the same context and use the defined epsilon near zero variance. Mixing requests confounds different reward difficulties. Category and residual codes must share the legal vocabulary interface.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Five high rewards for an easy request must not lower all advantages for a hard request; compare candidates within their own request.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.14434">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.14434-cq-sid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-11cee61cb6af22a3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:diffureason" data-paper-title="DiffuReason: Bridging Latent Reasoning and Generative Refinement for Sequential Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-diffureason-5f379d3c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a862bbd127f5ec07">Why denoise DiffuReason&#x27;s continuous Thinking Tokens rather than generating a long language rationale?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adiffureason">DiffuReason: Bridging Latent Reasoning and Generative Refinement for Sequential Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Continuous variables can hold several interest cues and be revised from history without language decoding at each step. Discrete ranking reward aligns the internal process through policy training. Latents are not automatically readable reasons, and iteration does not guarantee conflict resolution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A vector may adjust novelty and budget preferences without a textual explanation proving each choice.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.09744">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.09744-diffureason/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a862bbd127f5ec07">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:diffureason" data-paper-title="DiffuReason: Bridging Latent Reasoning and Generative Refinement for Sequential Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-fc1bd647de874fa4">Why does DiffuReason iteratively refine latent intent through diffusion instead of predicting one final recommendation representation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adiffureason">DiffuReason: Bridging Latent Reasoning and Generative Refinement for Sequential Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One prediction can compress conflicting interests into an unstable direction. Latent Thinking Tokens carry intent and iterative denoising revisits cues; GRPO aligns continuous generation with discrete ranking feedback. Extra steps cost compute and can accumulate bias; a local proxy does not establish full latent reasoning capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Fitness and dessert signals can be reconciled for a request without interpreting intermediate vectors as literal human thoughts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.09744">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.09744-diffureason/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fc1bd647de874fa4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:diffureason" data-paper-title="DiffuReason: Bridging Latent Reasoning and Generative Refinement for Sequential Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ab604647335a9b32">What benefits and serving costs does DiffuReason&#x27;s iterative update assume versus a one-shot user vector?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adiffureason">DiffuReason: Bridging Latent Reasoning and Generative Refinement for Sequential Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Denoising can revisit history at intermediate states, adding iteration cost and sampling uncertainty. Repeating the same bias need not help. Keep public proxies separate from actual diffusion policy training; a final score cannot verify the full path.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Later steps might correct an initial popularity bias if niche evidence is available, but ten steps cannot invent evidence missing from conditioning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.09744">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.09744-diffureason/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ab604647335a9b32">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:diffureason" data-paper-title="DiffuReason: Bridging Latent Reasoning and Generative Refinement for Sequential Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-9a5e8953cc6bda38">Why is a fixed reward added to final scores insufficient to implement DiffuReason denoising and GRPO?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adiffureason">DiffuReason: Bridging Latent Reasoning and Generative Refinement for Sequential Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Denoising needs defined timesteps, state transitions, and noise. Policy updates need same-context rollouts, rewards, and matching probabilities. A score addition does not train the continuous generation distribution or establish gradients. Local proxies do not replace end-to-end evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Multiplying popularity by 0.1 changes ranking but not latent denoising. Verify trajectories and real parameter updates before claiming policy training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.09744">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.09744-diffureason/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9a5e8953cc6bda38">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dualgr" data-paper-title="DualGR: Generative Retrieval with Long and Short-Term Interests Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-dualgr-b1420088" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c504ff33f2e6164e">Why does DualGR keep separate short- and long-term generation distributions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adualgr">DualGR: Generative Retrieval with Long and Short-Term Interests Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · USTC / Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A single compressed representation can let more numerous historical events dominate current needs. Separate learned paths are dynamically mixed with valid-prefix and exposure constraints, not simply duplicated vectors or a guarantee of detecting every new interest.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Keep established photography interest and new baby-product demand distinct enough to adjust their weights.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.12518">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2511.12518-dualgr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c504ff33f2e6164e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dualgr" data-paper-title="DualGR: Generative Retrieval with Long and Short-Term Interests Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-24d3da30a1a5d844">Why route long- and short-term interests separately in DualGR instead of concatenating history?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adualgr">DualGR: Generative Retrieval with Long and Short-Term Interests Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · USTC / Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Recent and stable interests matter differently by request. Two paths learn generation distributions, a gate mixes them conditionally, valid prefixes map outputs to items, and exposure terms limit dominance of popular codes. Check distinct learning and gate collapse.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A long travel history should not drown out today&#x27;s repeated kitchen-shopping actions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.12518">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2511.12518-dualgr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-24d3da30a1a5d844">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dualgr" data-paper-title="DualGR: Generative Retrieval with Long and Short-Term Interests Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-884b6556aed9923b">What freedom does DualGR&#x27;s two-path routing add over fixed exponential decay?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adualgr">DualGR: Generative Retrieval with Long and Short-Term Interests Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · USTC / Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixed decay prescribes how age changes influence. Separate learned statistics and request-level gating can adapt nonlinearly, with more parameters and calibration. Recent noise or stale long-term interests can still dominate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One accidental click and a burst of consistent demand can receive different gate responses that are hard to express with one decay rate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.12518">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2511.12518-dualgr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-884b6556aed9923b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dualgr" data-paper-title="DualGR: Generative Retrieval with Long and Short-Term Interests Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d3bcd19f48d36e04">Why align item columns before mixing the two DualGR distributions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adualgr">DualGR: Generative Retrieval with Long and Short-Term Interests Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · USTC / Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Gate-weighted addition needs probabilities for the same item IDs. Align codebooks and candidates, map legal prefixes to serving items, and derive exposure only from training-available data. Local proxies do not cover production routing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If column one means camera on one path and children&#x27;s clothes on the other, adding the values is semantically invalid despite matching shapes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.12518">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2511.12518-dualgr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d3bcd19f48d36e04">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:egr" data-paper-title="EGR: Embedding-Native Generative Retrieval with a Shared LLM" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-egr-a66d7f0c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-544a8e3547557490">Why jointly optimize item representation learning and next-item prediction in EGR?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aegr">EGR: Embedding-Native Generative Retrieval with a Shared LLM</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Snap Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Pure content optimization can omit recommendation distinctions. Next-item supervision retains consumption relationships while the item objective anchors semantics. Shared updates reduce separation but can conflict and do not guarantee alignment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Similar-genre movies can appeal to different audiences; joint learning can preserve that difference beyond text similarity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.23038">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.23038-egr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-544a8e3547557490">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:egr" data-paper-title="EGR: Embedding-Native Generative Retrieval with a Shared LLM" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-72f235af74f628cc">Why does EGR jointly train two tasks despite sharing the backbone for item indexing and user queries?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aegr">EGR: Embedding-Native Generative Retrieval with a Shared LLM</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Snap Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Shared parameters alone do not align retrieval geometry. Item representation learning maintains indexable content; next-item prediction directs queries toward consumption relations. Training one side against a changing other can stale the index, and serving and evaluation must use matching versions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If new item vectors rotate while queries stay in old coordinates, nearest neighbors can break despite matching dimensions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.23038">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.23038-egr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-72f235af74f628cc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:egr" data-paper-title="EGR: Embedding-Native Generative Retrieval with a Shared LLM" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-aebfbc8434aabce5">What deployment trade-off does EGR joint updating make versus freezing the item encoder?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aegr">EGR: Embedding-Native Generative Retrieval with a Shared LLM</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Snap Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Freezing stabilizes the index but blocks user supervision from refining item geometry. Joint learning can adapt both sides, requiring item refresh and versioned serving. The local negative result should not be replaced by the design promise.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A new query direction for science fiction may not match an old index; freezing avoids drift but keeps old limitations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.23038">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.23038-egr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-aebfbc8434aabce5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:egr" data-paper-title="EGR: Embedding-Native Generative Retrieval with a Shared LLM" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-239efdbe5c28d9d1">Why verify item-index and query versions after EGR updates its shared backbone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aegr">EGR: Embedding-Native Generative Retrieval with a Shared LLM</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Snap Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Updates can change dot-product meaning, so old index vectors may not match new queries. Record rebuild, training, and cutover boundaries and confirm both IRL and NIP run. A shared class name with one loss disabled is not joint training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An old item coordinate system and a new user coordinate system can have equal shapes but incompatible scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.23038">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.23038-egr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-239efdbe5c28d9d1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:feedback-policy" data-paper-title="From Understanding to Action: Feedback-Grounded Policy Discovery for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-feedback-policy-7fbe9a73" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-2df110b970fb5442">Why turn Feedback Policy feedback into relational supervision rather than caching strategy text?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Afeedback-policy">From Understanding to Action: Feedback-Grounded Policy Discovery for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huazhong Agricultural University (Kuaishou internship)</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Feedback reveals similarity and substitution structures that a lightweight model can learn from a relation matrix without online LLM explanations. The matrix is a teacher proxy with possible bias and incomplete reasoning. Text storage alone does not update model behavior.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Learning that two tutorials are substitutes can prevent them dominating a list; a note to diversify does not change embeddings.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27789">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.27789-feedback-policy/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2df110b970fb5442">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:feedback-policy" data-paper-title="From Understanding to Action: Feedback-Grounded Policy Discovery for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-3d327498079e2bb6">Why does Feedback Policy distill teacher relations instead of only independent item scores?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Afeedback-policy">From Understanding to Action: Feedback-Grounded Policy Discovery for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huazhong Agricultural University (Kuaishou internship)</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Knowledge also resides in candidate similarities and preferences. Relation matching transfers feedback-derived structure to a lightweight ranker without serving an LLM. Teacher biases can transfer, and smaller matrix error need not improve user feedback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two similarly scored products can be substitutes for a request. Capturing that relation informs list composition beyond copying static scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27789">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.27789-feedback-policy/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3d327498079e2bb6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:feedback-policy" data-paper-title="From Understanding to Action: Feedback-Grounded Policy Discovery for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-0876b9b0cd20266d">How do relation-matrix and per-item logit distillation emphasize different errors?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Afeedback-policy">From Understanding to Action: Feedback-Grounded Policy Discovery for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huazhong Agricultural University (Kuaishou internship)</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Logits match absolute outputs; matrices match relative layouts and can be less sensitive to global scale shifts. Structural matching can miss probability calibration. Compare under a fixed protocol rather than assuming more constraints improve quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Adding a constant to all teacher scores leaves order intact but changes independent errors; relative distillation need not constrain absolute click probability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27789">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.27789-feedback-policy/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0876b9b0cd20266d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:feedback-policy" data-paper-title="From Understanding to Action: Feedback-Grounded Policy Discovery for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-bbcf875d87142580">Why use the same identity order for teacher and student relation matrices?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Afeedback-policy">From Understanding to Action: Feedback-Grounded Policy Discovery for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huazhong Agricultural University (Kuaishou internship)</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Every cell denotes a specific pair, so wrong ordering fits wrong relationships despite equal shapes. Match valid entries, normalization, and padding masks and use allowed evidence. The local proxy does not validate the complete real-user feedback loop.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Camera in teacher row two and novel in student row two is an invalid comparison; align by item ID first.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27789">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.27789-feedback-policy/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bbcf875d87142580">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:gear" data-paper-title="Generative End-to-end Ad Retrieval at Douyin" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-gear-42599d59" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-779db58082983dba">Why do GEAR BasisVQ and BasisRQ represent codes in a shared orthogonal basis?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agear">Generative End-to-end Ad Retrieval at Douyin</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A common basis coordinates updates; orthogonality constrains rotation so codewords do not drift independently. Hierarchical generation supplies addresses and context reranks collisions. Orthogonality does not guarantee semantic independence or collision-free coding; test quantization and ranking separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two similar items can still share a bucket despite a stable coordinate system.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
