<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:gear" data-paper-title="Generative End-to-end Ad Retrieval at Douyin" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-97a87993f2fd04a0">Why does GEAR use a shared orthogonal basis instead of freely updating each code vector?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agear">Generative End-to-end Ad Retrieval at Douyin</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A shared basis constrains codebook geometry and stabilizes relationships as it changes. Hierarchical generation selects coarse-to-fine codes, then context reranks collision groups. Structure neither eliminates collisions nor replaces ranking supervision. Local checks cover quantization, state, and gradients, not full ad retrieval.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Update codes within one coordinate system, but still distinguish two ads in the same code with current user context.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.39327">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.39327-gear/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-97a87993f2fd04a0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:gear" data-paper-title="Generative End-to-end Ad Retrieval at Douyin" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-31adb8cf73ce4e1d">How does GEAR&#x27;s collision reranker allocate discrimination differently from indefinitely enlarging the codebook?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agear">Generative End-to-end Ad Retrieval at Douyin</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Larger vocabularies distinguish more items at discrete addresses. Reranking keeps finite codes and resolves within-bucket candidates using user context, saving code capacity but adding bucket compute and recall limits. Local mechanism checks and orthogonality errors do not measure recommendation quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Rerank two same-code cameras by user needs rather than assigning unique large-vocabulary codes; oversized buckets still cost compute.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.39327">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.39327-gear/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-31adb8cf73ce4e1d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:gear" data-paper-title="Generative End-to-end Ad Retrieval at Douyin" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-2eaf29cb6ed10361">Why align row-vector conventions and check B&#x27;s orthogonality for GEAR&#x27;s zB and inverse mapping?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agear">Generative End-to-end Ad Retrieval at Douyin</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Projection, nearest-code selection, and reconstruction must use consistent transposes; equal square shapes can hide mistakes. Verify orthogonality, residual quantization, and collision mapping separately. Diagnostics do not cover production generator quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>After multiplying a row by B, reconstruct using the corresponding inverse, and test the round trip on a known vector.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.39327">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.39327-gear/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2eaf29cb6ed10361">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:genrec" data-paper-title="GenRec: A Preference-Oriented Generative Framework for Large-Scale Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-genrec-e5f875fa" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-2f8db993ea0b2837">Why organize consecutive positives as a next-page target in GenRec?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agenrec">GenRec: A Preference-Oriented Generative Framework for Large-Scale Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · JD.com</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Within-page consumption has order and complementarity that point prediction misses. Generate with prefix dependence and score the entire page with grouped rewards. Pages assembled from consecutive public actions are proxies, not observed impression pages.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Tent, sleeping bag, and pad can form a useful page; three consecutive movie views do not prove simultaneous display.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.14878">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2604.14878-genrec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2f8db993ea0b2837">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:genrec" data-paper-title="GenRec: A Preference-Oriented Generative Framework for Large-Scale Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-e1b9b517b34000d1">Why does GenRec target a next-page sequence and keep NLL alongside GRPO?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agenrec">GenRec: A Preference-Oriented Generative Framework for Large-Scale Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · JD.com</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Item targets alone do not teach order and complementarity within pages. Sequence targets model composition, group-relative reward shapes full-page utility, and NLL anchors to logged behavior against reward drift. Rewards that omit relevance or feasibility can still mislead.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A page objective can replace one of three redundant items; an NLL anchor can restrain a novelty-only reward from recommending irrelevant content.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.14878">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2604.14878-genrec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e1b9b517b34000d1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:genrec" data-paper-title="GenRec: A Preference-Oriented Generative Framework for Large-Scale Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-c79d1223eeb4334a">What drift does GenRec&#x27;s NLL limit compared with optimizing GRPO-SR reward alone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agenrec">GenRec: A Preference-Oriented Generative Framework for Large-Scale Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · JD.com</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Group-relative rewards compare page utility while NLL preserves logged behavior, limiting drift toward sparse or biased rewards. Their balance trades imitation for exploration. Local relative gains depend on proxy labels and baseline and do not establish real satisfaction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Diversity reward alone can produce irrelevant novelty; NLL retains basic interests.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.14878">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2604.14878-genrec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c79d1223eeb4334a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:genrec" data-paper-title="GenRec: A Preference-Oriented Generative Framework for Large-Scale Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-071c67569a5ee13d">Why compare GenRec page advantages only within the same context?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agenrec">GenRec: A Preference-Oriented Generative Framework for Large-Scale Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · JD.com</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Same-context pages share history and candidate difficulty, so mean subtraction measures relative quality. Mixing users confounds request difficulty. Update prefix and duplicate masks together, apply NLL to legal targets, and do not use Token Merger to expose future test pages.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Compare pages within each photography or cold-start user rather than marking every harder request negative.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.14878">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2604.14878-genrec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-071c67569a5ee13d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:glide" data-paper-title="Deploying Semantic ID-based Generative Retrieval for Large-Scale Podcast Discovery at Spotify" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-glide-1ae86d8e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0cbf0ecf4df68a6c">Why separate GLIDE&#x27;s recent behavior and long-term embeddings into two prompt types?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aglide">Deploying Semantic ID-based Generative Retrieval for Large-Scale Podcast Discovery at Spotify</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Spotify</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The sequence retains immediate details; the embedding summarizes stable preferences. Separate inputs avoid averaging them together. Hierarchical SID paths still depend on prompt and codebook coverage; their combination does not prove reduced filter bubbles.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Preserve long-term photography and recent camping signals to support outdoor cameras or campsite gear.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.17540">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.17540-glide/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0cbf0ecf4df68a6c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:glide" data-paper-title="Deploying Semantic ID-based Generative Retrieval for Large-Scale Podcast Discovery at Spotify" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-0b2de1129245e709">Why does GLIDE use separate prompts for recent behavior and long-term user embeddings?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aglide">Deploying Semantic ID-based Generative Retrieval for Large-Scale Podcast Discovery at Spotify</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Spotify</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Recent behavior captures immediate intent but can repeatedly favor familiar items. The long-term representation adds stable preferences missed by a short window. Both condition SID generation, trading responsiveness and exploration; long-term features can go stale and do not establish exploration by themselves.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Recent commute podcasts can inform context while stable science interest helps discover a new science show.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.17540">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.17540-glide/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0b2de1129245e709">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:glide" data-paper-title="Deploying Semantic ID-based Generative Retrieval for Large-Scale Podcast Discovery at Spotify" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e7e19c426f1e5e87">How does GLIDE&#x27;s dual-prompt generation change outputs compared with transition or content retrieval?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aglide">Deploying Semantic ID-based Generative Retrieval for Large-Scale Podcast Discovery at Spotify</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Spotify</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Traditional systems directly combine similarity or transition scores. GLIDE predicts conditioned SID-path probabilities and maps them to candidates, sharing semantics through discrete codes while adding quantization and early-path errors. A local code-transition proxy does not train the full language generator.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Generate a photography coarse code then refine it. Choosing the wrong branch can exclude a target that full-catalog scoring could still rank.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.17540">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.17540-glide/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e7e19c426f1e5e87">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:glide" data-paper-title="Deploying Semantic ID-based Generative Retrieval for Large-Scale Podcast Discovery at Spotify" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c75b3e3a99ba4ee5">Why must GLIDE&#x27;s long-term embedding exclude the complete post-test user history?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aglide">Deploying Semantic ID-based Generative Retrieval for Large-Scale Podcast Discovery at Spotify</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Spotify</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Both long-term summaries and recent sequences must stop at available behavior. A test target inside the long-term vector leaks even if absent from recent inputs. Document codebook fitting and the local three-level public proxy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A movie&#x27;s vector cannot contribute to the history used to predict that same held-out movie.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.17540">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.17540-glide/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c75b3e3a99ba4ee5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:gr4ad" data-paper-title="Generative Recommendation for Large-Scale Advertising" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-gr4ad-4d146b97" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-5b9317365ed4f756">Why does GR4AD address commercial SIDs, generation dependencies, and beam budgets under load?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agr4ad">Generative Recommendation for Large-Scale Advertising</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Ads need relevance, business attributes, fast updates, and bounded latency. UA-SID provides multi-granularity codes, LazyAR relaxes sequential dependencies, value/list training aligns utility, and dynamic beams manage serving cost. Next-code accuracy cannot measure all four.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An excellent ad is unusable if decoding is too slow, while overly narrow beams can miss it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.22732">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.22732-gr4ad/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5b9317365ed4f756">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:gr4ad" data-paper-title="Generative Recommendation for Large-Scale Advertising" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1aaa4f6709186ebb">Why does GR4AD combine business-value weighting and list optimization rather than only predicting the next ad code?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agr4ad">Generative Recommendation for Large-Scale Advertising</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Next-token imitation can favor frequent low-value ads. Value weighting changes sample contribution; list objectives model relative business utility. Multi-granularity SIDs and relaxed dependencies address separate representation and compute issues. Check relevance and head concentration rather than reporting only revenue proxies.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A rare high-value ad may matter more than a frequently shown low-conversion one; frequency imitation alone misses that.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.22732">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.22732-gr4ad/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1aaa4f6709186ebb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:gr4ad" data-paper-title="Generative Recommendation for Large-Scale Advertising" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-683a274918c2779d">Why are GR4AD VSL and RSPO respectively weighted supervision and list alignment?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agr4ad">Generative Recommendation for Large-Scale Advertising</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>VSL emphasizes high-value examples in code-prediction loss; RSPO reshapes within-list preferences using a reward distribution. They act at different granularities but may jointly concentrate exposure. Report concentration alongside NDCG, particularly when local value is proxied by popularity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Upweighting costly items and redistributing list probabilities by reward can both increase head exposure.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:gr4ad" data-paper-title="Generative Recommendation for Large-Scale Advertising" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-8bae8a9f22f76a35">Why align GR4AD RSPO&#x27;s `q_j∝exp(r_j/τ)` with the candidate probability space?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agr4ad">Generative Recommendation for Large-Scale Advertising</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Normalize within one context&#x27;s legal candidates and compute cross-entropy against identical student candidate identities. Temperature controls sharpness; ordering, invalid items, and cross-request groups change the target. Public value proxies are not eCPM, and these losses do not verify full LazyAR or dynamic serving.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If q column two is a camera and student column two is children&#x27;s clothes, gradients are wrong even if q sums to one.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.22732">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.22732-gr4ad/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8bae8a9f22f76a35">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:grc" data-paper-title="Learning to Reflect and Correct: Towards Better Decoding Trajectories for Large-Scale Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-grc-7f75523b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-22487c67ad9da2a1">Why structure GRC trajectories as draft, reflection, and corrected SID?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agrc">Learning to Reflect and Correct: Towards Better Decoding Trajectories for Large-Scale Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International / Wuhan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Early hierarchical mistakes restrict later choices. Explicit steps teach locating and repairing deviations instead of only imitating correct codes. At inference the model must identify errors itself, and valid formatting does not guarantee effective correction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Switch a home-goods draft to cameras by recognizing the request evidence, not by seeing a gold first-error index.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.23639">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.23639-grc/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-22487c67ad9da2a1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:grc" data-paper-title="Learning to Reflect and Correct: Towards Better Decoding Trajectories for Large-Scale Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-34cb5a2e2828c895">Why can&#x27;t a GRC corrector read the first wrong SID position during evaluation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agrc">Learning to Reflect and Correct: Towards Better Decoding Trajectories for Large-Scale Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International / Wuhan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Gold codes only build training draft–reflection–correction supervision. Deployment must infer likely errors from candidates, attribute consistency, and uncertainty without answer leakage. Entropy allocates correction budget, but hard high-entropy cases need not improve.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A training example can identify a wrong city code; live recommendation cannot know the user&#x27;s eventual target code.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.23639">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.23639-grc/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-34cb5a2e2828c895">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:grc" data-paper-title="Learning to Reflect and Correct: Towards Better Decoding Trajectories for Large-Scale Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-c072daa2eaad153e">What does GRC trade by allocating correction to uncertainty rather than fixing every beam equally?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agrc">Learning to Reflect and Correct: Towards Better Decoding Trajectories for Large-Scale Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International / Wuhan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reflection-token entropy prioritizes likely repair candidates under a fixed budget, reducing duplicate work. High entropy can be noise and low entropy can be confidently wrong. The reported reward rose but test ranking fell; retain both.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Correct two uncertain beams out of ten first, while recognizing that a confident wrong path might be missed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.23639">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.23639-grc/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c072daa2eaad153e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:grc" data-paper-title="Learning to Reflect and Correct: Towards Better Decoding Trajectories for Large-Scale Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-bd4e3f5d3c957901">How should GRC separate training first-error labels from test reflection inputs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agrc">Learning to Reflect and Correct: Towards Better Decoding Trajectories for Large-Scale Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International / Wuhan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Compare drafts with gold during training and use `L+1` if all levels match. At test, use only model drafts, attributes, and uncertainty. Bind reflection, correction, and reward to one trajectory without gold-based repairs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Giving the second-level gold mismatch to the test corrector makes it an answer-aware diagnostic, not autonomous repair.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.23639">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.23639-grc/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bd4e3f5d3c957901">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:growthgr" data-paper-title="Towards Sustainable Growth: A Multi-Value-Aware Retrieval Framework for E-Commerce Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-growthgr-aa9df061" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-caed8bc40762fb5b">Why use ItemLTV instead of immediate new-item purchases in GrowthGR?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agrowthgr">Towards Sustainable Growth: A Multi-Value-Aware Retrieval Framework for E-Commerce Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group / Taobao &amp; Tmall</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Low initial exposure leads to few immediate purchases and can hide effects of first clicks on later orders. ItemLTV separates baseline and increment; MoPO aligns generation with multiple behavioral goals. Predicted incremental value is not inherently causal without credible assumptions and feedback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A click today might lead to a later series purchase despite no same-day conversion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.17994">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.17994-growthgr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-caed8bc40762fb5b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:growthgr" data-paper-title="Towards Sustainable Growth: A Multi-Value-Aware Retrieval Framework for E-Commerce Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-fcd351b4112088fb">Why does GrowthGR use ItemLTV incremental value and multi-objective post-training instead of only increasing new-item exposure?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agrowthgr">Towards Sustainable Growth: A Multi-Value-Aware Retrieval Framework for E-Commerce Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group / Taobao &amp; Tmall</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Exposure is a means, not an outcome. ItemLTV estimates changes in future orders or value relative to what would happen anyway; multi-objective training balances click, purchase, and coverage. Clip rare high-value weights to limit instability. Counterfactual assumptions and rewards need validation; more new items do not prove growth.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A first exposure can open a sustained use case or cause one accidental click; equal traffic treats these differently valuable opportunities alike.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.17994">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.17994-growthgr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fcd351b4112088fb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:growthgr" data-paper-title="Towards Sustainable Growth: A Multi-Value-Aware Retrieval Framework for E-Commerce Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b6962cf96eaddecd">How do GrowthGR rare high-value weights differ from a uniform novelty reward?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agrowthgr">Towards Sustainable Growth: A Multi-Value-Aware Retrieval Framework for E-Commerce Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group / Taobao &amp; Tmall</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A novelty reward uses newness alone. Rarity weights use previous-policy probability and multi-objective value to emphasize potentially useful low-opportunity items. Low probability is not quality; clipping limits amplified noise. Neither alone proves growth.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two new items with little exposure should not get identical boosts if estimated long-term relevance differs, though a bad estimate can be amplified.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.17994">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.17994-growthgr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b6962cf96eaddecd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:growthgr" data-paper-title="Towards Sustainable Growth: A Multi-Value-Aware Retrieval Framework for E-Commerce Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-0acfd97ef595f1da">Why clip GrowthGR rarity weights based on `−log πold` and fix the reference policy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agrowthgr">Towards Sustainable Growth: A Multi-Value-Aware Retrieval Framework for E-Commerce Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group / Taobao &amp; Tmall</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Tiny old probabilities create extreme weights, high variance, and single-sample dominance. πold must match the sample&#x27;s generating policy and context, not current probabilities. Policy ratios and reward weights have different roles; separate ItemLTV proxies from real orders.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Clipping can stop one noisy low-probability example from dominating a batch without making its value estimate reliable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.17994">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.17994-growthgr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0acfd97ef595f1da">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:grp" data-paper-title="GRP v0.1 Technical Report" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-grp-12c5e416" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-e4195cdb964d413c">Why migrate GRP&#x27;s recommendation funnel gradually instead of replacing all stages at once?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agrp">GRP v0.1 Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Snap Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Established systems serve several goals and risks. Introduce an additional retrieval source, replace weak sources, increase quota, and then bypass ranking progressively. Keep original recall protections and separate evidence and permissions per stage; a unified design is not a finished rollout.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Start with a small candidate share and expand only after validation rather than removing retrieval and fine ranking on one offline win.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36688">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.36688-grp/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e4195cdb964d413c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:grp" data-paper-title="GRP v0.1 Technical Report" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-7c1a13612a425df6">Why activate GRP&#x27;s one-sided logged-target margin only when original-target retrieval suffers?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agrp">GRP v0.1 Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Snap Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reward optimization can move mass to a few high-reward outputs and lower logged-target probability. Penalize decreases past tolerance while permitting other improvements. Freeze and stop gradients through the ranking reward head to prevent co-adaptation. Local objectives and gradients do not verify production funnel replacement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Improve new candidates without a penalty if the original target remains competitive; penalize shifting all mass to one high-reward category.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36688">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.36688-grp/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7c1a13612a425df6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:grp" data-paper-title="GRP v0.1 Technical Report" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-094cd821bb640a1f">What freedom does GRP&#x27;s one-sided margin retain compared with symmetric probability constraints?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agrp">GRP v0.1 Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Snap Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Only a logged-target drop beyond reference tolerance incurs penalty, leaving other preference improvements free. Symmetric constraints may suppress beneficial changes too. Target preservation does not validate the new reward, and local checks only cover surrogate objectives and gradients.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Raise better candidates while preserving the logged target without penalty; a large abandonment of that target activates the guard.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36688">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.36688-grp/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-094cd821bb640a1f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:grp" data-paper-title="GRP v0.1 Technical Report" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-5ccd8a0812b61c8e">Why does GRP&#x27;s MHP ranking head read detached generator representations?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agrp">GRP v0.1 Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Snap Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Ranking gradients through shared encoding and SID paths can damage existing retrieval. Stop-gradient trains the ranker without changing the generator from this loss. Version it when frozen as RL reward and verify actual gradient separation rather than only registration.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Updating ranking BCE should change the head but not send gradients into the SID-generation backbone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36688">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.36688-grp/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5ccd8a0812b61c8e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:gryphon-v2" data-paper-title="Gryphon-v2: One Model in Place of a Cascade — Generate-and-Rank Recommender with Rollout Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-gryphon-v2-65508cc1" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a1a741eb904c4131">Why do Gryphon-v2&#x27;s generation and ranking heads share a history encoder?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agryphon-v2">Gryphon-v2: One Model in Place of a Cascade — Generate-and-Rank Recommender with Rollout Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Yandex</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Re-encoding the same history wastes computation and can produce inconsistent user states. A shared encoder supports SID nomination and ranking, but the ranker still depends on the generated candidate set and cannot recover omissions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Both heads see a user&#x27;s recent switch to jazz, but missing jazz items cannot be reranked.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06213">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.06213-gryphon-v2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a1a741eb904c4131">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:gryphon-v2" data-paper-title="Gryphon-v2: One Model in Place of a Cascade — Generate-and-Rank Recommender with Rollout Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-68390dcde3890556">Why distill both current rollouts and actual exposure candidates in Gryphon-v2?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agryphon-v2">Gryphon-v2: One Model in Place of a Cascade — Generate-and-Rank Recommender with Rollout Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Yandex</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A changing generator proposes items rare in old logs; exposure-only training may not score its outputs well. Rollout-only training discards established coverage. One teacher calibrates both distributions, and a shared encoder links generation and ranking. Teacher bias can still transfer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Rollout supervision covers niche movies proposed by the new generator, while real exposures preserve knowledge of existing popular ones.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06213">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.06213-gryphon-v2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-68390dcde3890556">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:gryphon-v2" data-paper-title="Gryphon-v2: One Model in Place of a Cascade — Generate-and-Rank Recommender with Rollout Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-98e08b58f6a6ac4b">Why does dual-source distillation better reflect generator serving candidates than logged impressions alone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agryphon-v2">Gryphon-v2: One Model in Place of a Cascade — Generate-and-Rank Recommender with Rollout Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Yandex</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Old impressions are policy-selected and can miss the current rollout distribution. Combined training sees actual exposure evidence plus the generator&#x27;s outputs. The teacher may be unreliable in new regions; the local comparison was negative despite broader coverage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Niche instrumental candidates missing from old logs get rollout supervision, but can inherit teacher bias.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06213">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.06213-gryphon-v2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-98e08b58f6a6ac4b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:gryphon-v2" data-paper-title="Gryphon-v2: One Model in Place of a Cascade — Generate-and-Rank Recommender with Rollout Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-66abe065a27702a3">Why keep Gryphon-v2 rollout and impression distillation provenance separate?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agryphon-v2">Gryphon-v2: One Model in Place of a Cascade — Generate-and-Rank Recommender with Rollout Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Yandex</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Counts, weights, and candidate identities from different distributions affect the loss. Compare teacher and student on matching items and cutoffs and track which source dominates. Both objectives updated locally, but quality regressed; updates are not gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Sixty thousand distilled rollout items are not 60,000 real impressions and must not be labeled user clicks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06213">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.06213-gryphon-v2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-66abe065a27702a3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:guess-where-you-go" data-paper-title="Guess Where You Go: Generative Next Point-of-Interest Recommendation in Amap" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-guess-where-you-go-0a00ce9c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-5c0182623a051bb9">Why does next-POI generation rely on spatiotemporal context more than content recommendation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aguess-where-you-go">Guess Where You Go: Generative Next Point-of-Interest Recommendation in Amap</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Amap / Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Current area, time, accessibility, opening hours, and trip stage affect destinations. SIDs represent places; context selects meaningful paths. Pure co-occurrence can recommend semantically related but unreachable places.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A lunchtime request in Shanghai should favor nearby food, not a favorite Beijing café.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.26073">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.26073-guess-where-you-go/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5c0182623a051bb9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:guess-where-you-go" data-paper-title="Guess Where You Go: Generative Next Point-of-Interest Recommendation in Amap" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-51385eee77e0ff0e">Why does next-POI generation need spatiotemporal context rather than ordinary place IDs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aguess-where-you-go">Guess Where You Go: Generative Next Point-of-Interest Recommendation in Amap</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Amap / Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Distance, time, and travel state constrain feasibility. Hierarchical semantic IDs organize places, contextual features constrain present needs, and curriculum training adds more complex feedback gradually. Long-horizon rewards need actual observations; co-occurrence or one hit does not establish route-planning value.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A coffee lover can reach different shops on a morning commute and a weekend trip.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.26073">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.26073-guess-where-you-go/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-51385eee77e0ff0e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:guess-where-you-go" data-paper-title="Guess Where You Go: Generative Next Point-of-Interest Recommendation in Amap" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-36999f29a5d3cc4f">What stages do curriculum pretraining/SFT and long-term POI policy updates address?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aguess-where-you-go">Guess Where You Go: Generative Next Point-of-Interest Recommendation in Amap</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Amap / Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Curriculum and supervision establish place semantics, timing, spatial relationships, and generation; later feedback adjusts long-term preference without exploring a huge space from sparse reward alone. Public movie proxies do not verify mobility or POI capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Learn legal regions and visit sequences first, then refine routes based on satisfaction rather than expecting one reward to teach city geography.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.26073">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.26073-guess-where-you-go/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-36999f29a5d3cc4f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:guess-where-you-go" data-paper-title="Guess Where You Go: Generative Next Point-of-Interest Recommendation in Amap" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6eb83c37777015f5">Which POI SID training targets must not become request features?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aguess-where-you-go">Guess Where You Go: Generative Next Point-of-Interest Recommendation in Amap</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Amap / Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Target locations and future stay feedback can enter loss only. Inputs use prior trajectories and contemporaneous context, not next-stop coordinates for filtering. Codes map to the matching directory version, and proxy score fusion is not full policy training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Filtering by the true destination&#x27;s shopping district leaks the answer; use the user&#x27;s current area and legal constraints.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.26073">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.26073-guess-where-you-go/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6eb83c37777015f5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:hrpo" data-paper-title="Hierarchical Residual Policy Optimization for Generative Recommendations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-hrpo-d54751e8" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-957dac4052db66ef">Why does HRPO decompose prefix utility into residual credits?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ahrpo">Hierarchical Residual Policy Optimization for Generative Recommendations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · City University of Hong Kong / Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Final item rewards are sparse, and giving all SID tokens the same score obscures which steps contribute. Differences in prefix utility supply the marginal credit of a newly added code, and credit-to-go accumulates later effects for earlier decisions. Smoothing depends on user clusters and estimation quality; a difference is not a directly observed causal contribution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: The first token correctly chooses outdoor goods, but the next goes to irrelevant decoration. The two can receive different feedback despite the same failed final outcome.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.00750">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.00750-hrpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-957dac4052db66ef">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:hrpo" data-paper-title="Hierarchical Residual Policy Optimization for Generative Recommendations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d24dff680526ea54">Why does HRPO split the final reward into prefix residual credit and credit-to-go?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ahrpo">Hierarchical Residual Policy Optimization for Generative Recommendations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · City University of Hong Kong / Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Broadcasting a whole-item reward to each SID token assigns identical responsibility to distinct decisions and can raise variance. HRPO smooths prefix utilities within user clusters, takes differences between neighboring prefixes as local credit, and accumulates subsequent credit so earlier decisions can learn their longer-term effects. Prefix utility is estimated: the decomposition does not automatically remove bias, and inference cannot read the true target path.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: The first code can choose the wrong category and doom the entire path, while the last only refines a choice within the category. Prefix credit tries to distinguish those roles rather than treating all codes alike.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.00750">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.00750-hrpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d24dff680526ea54">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:hrpo" data-paper-title="Hierarchical Residual Policy Optimization for Generative Recommendations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1fdb54974977027f">How does credit-to-go differ from using only each token&#x27;s own delta in HRPO?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ahrpo">Hierarchical Residual Policy Optimization for Generative Recommendations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · City University of Hong Kong / Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A single-step delta ignores how early choices constrain later ones. Credit-to-go sums residuals from the current step through the end, preserving long-term consequences. It can also accumulate estimation noise, and RRPO uses conservative updates to limit drift. The mechanism alone guarantees neither variance reduction nor an unbiased gradient of the original objective; those need a derivation for the specific case.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Choosing cameras early makes a good lens reachable later. Summing later credits lets the first token see that benefit, but an erroneous later utility can also propagate backward.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.00750">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.00750-hrpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1fdb54974977027f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:hrpo" data-paper-title="Hierarchical Residual Policy Optimization for Generative Recommendations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c344642547d511ac">How can a telescoping check verify HRPO&#x27;s prefix differences?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ahrpo">Hierarchical Residual Policy Optimization for Generative Recommendations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · City University of Hong Kong / Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Adjacent deltas should use the same version of utility. Their sum should equal final-prefix utility minus empty-prefix utility, and credit-to-go sums from the current position, not the start. User-cluster smoothing must not include future test feedback. The local binary SID verifies this bounded mechanism, not large-scale generative post-training performance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: If the empty-prefix utility is zero and the next three utilities are 1, 3, and 2, the deltas are 1, 2, and −1, which sum to 2. A different total from mixed smoothing tables exposes an inconsistency.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.00750">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.00750-hrpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c344642547d511ac">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:intsr" data-paper-title="IntSR: An Integrated Generative Framework for Search and Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-intsr-9d48eca1" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-e9621be987a8d381">Why combine explicit queries and implicit session intent in the same item space in IntSR?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aintsr">IntSR: An Integrated Generative Framework for Search and Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Amap</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Search terms can omit background, while session activity offers context without directly stating the current request. Joint intent inference uses both, and a shared vocabulary avoids fragmented item identities across the two entry points. Time represents drift. An absent query should follow a defined missing-input path, not be replaced with something the user supposedly said.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A query of &#x27;nearby&#x27; combined with a recent vegetarian search can suggest dining. A recommendation-only visit should use its session without inventing a user query.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.21179">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2509.21179-intsr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e9621be987a8d381">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:intsr" data-paper-title="IntSR: An Integrated Generative Framework for Search and Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-fb387442d699fb31">How does IntSR handle both explicit search terms and recommendation intent without a query?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aintsr">IntSR: An Integrated Generative Framework for Search and Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Amap</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>An explicit query expresses the current request; implicit session history supplies unspoken needs. Both inform latent intent, and results are generated in a unified item or POI vocabulary. Time context helps determine whether needs still apply and bridges search and recommendation. Sharing a vocabulary does not excuse ignoring query constraints or treating old interests as explicit current requests.</p>
