<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: When a user searches for nearby coffee, a history of quiet venues can supplement the query. With no search, the session can suggest a need, but yesterday&#x27;s location should not be assumed to apply today.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.21179">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2509.21179-intsr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fb387442d699fb31">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:intsr" data-paper-title="IntSR: An Integrated Generative Framework for Search and Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-42ca84522a89bc1e">What does IntSR&#x27;s latent-intent mixture make explicit compared with concatenating q and h for scoring?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aintsr">IntSR: An Integrated Generative Framework for Search and Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Amap</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It first estimates an intent distribution and then generates items conditioned on intent and time, keeping multiple plausible needs explicit. Direct concatenation may express this implicitly without learning the same structure. A latent variable need not have a stable human meaning, and a more decomposable output does not prove recovery of true intent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: &#x27;Weekend activities&#x27; could mean hiking or an exhibition. Keeping probabilities for both before choosing a venue is natural, but those probabilities remain model estimates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.21179">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2509.21179-intsr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-42ca84522a89bc1e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:intsr" data-paper-title="IntSR: An Integrated Generative Framework for Search and Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-3b3becae3d60389c">How should IntSR distinguish an absent query from a real empty-string search?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aintsr">IntSR: An Integrated Generative Framework for Search and Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Amap</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use the missingness marker or branch specified by the model contract. Time conditioning may only use the request timestamp, and the target POI must not enter latent-intent estimation. Both entry points share item identity, not necessarily every label. The source&#x27;s movie proxy cannot test real locations or opening hours.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Never starting a search and deliberately submitting a blank query can have different log meanings. Do not collapse them to one unexplained string and leave the model to guess.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.21179">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2509.21179-intsr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3b3becae3d60389c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:leadre" data-paper-title="LEADRE: Multi-Faceted Knowledge Enhanced LLM Empowered Display Advertisement Recommender System" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-leadre-72cfaef2" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-9a2a5492b043376d">Why combine cross-domain, long-term, and real-time behavior in LEADRE&#x27;s intent-aware prompt?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aleadre">LEADRE: Multi-Faceted Knowledge Enhanced LLM Empowered Display Advertisement Recommender System</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent / WeChat</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Cross-domain activity supplies clues unavailable in ads, long-term summaries retain stable interests, and real-time behavior reflects change. Together they help S-ID generation do more than memorize IDs. Summaries and caches can be stale and sources may conflict; a longer prompt is not full user understanding.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A stable photography preference, recent travel search, and current camera browsing suggest portable gear even if the new ad has no in-domain click history.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.13789">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2411.13789-leadre/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9a2a5492b043376d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:leadre" data-paper-title="LEADRE: Multi-Faceted Knowledge Enhanced LLM Empowered Display Advertisement Recommender System" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-cbbfe12497e2d087">Why train LEADRE ad SID generation with an intent prompt, semantic auxiliary tasks, and DPO?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aleadre">LEADRE: Multi-Faceted Knowledge Enhanced LLM Empowered Display Advertisement Recommender System</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent / WeChat</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Predicting only discrete codes can memorize exposed IDs instead of using ad content and cross-domain needs. The intent prompt organizes long-term and real-time signals; semantic and commercial value objectives make codes more useful; DPO adjusts preference trade-offs. Report SFT-to-DPO changes separately because preference tuning need not improve every retrieval metric.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Two appliance ads may differ in relevance to current renovation, even if one appears much more often. Semantic and value supervision can separate them, but too much DPO weight on commercial feedback may hurt new relevant candidates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.13789">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2411.13789-leadre/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cbbfe12497e2d087">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:leadre" data-paper-title="LEADRE: Multi-Faceted Knowledge Enhanced LLM Empowered Display Advertisement Recommender System" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1e6da910e42ba711">How can LEADRE&#x27;s full system improve while its DPO ablation worsens?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aleadre">LEADRE: Multi-Faceted Knowledge Enhanced LLM Empowered Display Advertisement Recommender System</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent / WeChat</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The full system changes SID and semantic/value auxiliary tasks, whereas the ablation adds preference updates to the same SFT. Beating DIN does not validate each change. The local DPO result regressed relative to SFT, so do not attribute the full gain to alignment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Pretraining may deliver a large gain, DPO may give some back, and the final system still beats a weaker baseline.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.13789">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2411.13789-leadre/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1e6da910e42ba711">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:leadre" data-paper-title="LEADRE: Multi-Faceted Knowledge Enhanced LLM Empowered Display Advertisement Recommender System" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-4b755cc139af50ae">Why must LEADRE keep the reference and context aligned when constructing winning and losing ad SID paths?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aleadre">LEADRE: Multi-Faceted Knowledge Enhanced LLM Empowered Display Advertisement Recommender System</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent / WeChat</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The objective compares winner and loser probability changes relative to a reference under the same user intent. Switching requests or references changes the target. Construct legal SID mappings and auxiliary labels at the cutoff, do not use test answers in prompts, and version long-term caches with real-time inputs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Two legal SID paths preferred by user A must not be scored against a reference conditioned on user B&#x27;s history.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.13789">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2411.13789-leadre/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4b755cc139af50ae">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mbgr" data-paper-title="MBGR: Multi-Business Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-mbgr-3a21e1da" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-2b13e572a09b32b8">Why look up the nearest future interaction separately for each business in MBGR?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ambgr">MBGR: Multi-Business Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A global next-item label covers only one business. LDR looks ahead per business so a shared state learns multiple directions and masks missing labels. Multi-task supervision does not let future events enter history.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A current state can learn about both the next short video and later shopping instead of letting abundant video labels drown out shopping.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.02684">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2604.02684-mbgr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2b13e572a09b32b8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mbgr" data-paper-title="MBGR: Multi-Business Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f28720ce81a7ef92">Why does MBGR find the nearest future event for each business rather than just supervising the next log event?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ambgr">MBGR: Multi-Business Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Interleaved streams let frequent businesses dominate adjacent labels. LDR finds each business&#x27;s nearest future target from a shared current state and conditions on business identity, exposing multiple prediction paths. Mask missing futures. This is training supervision only; future events are not current inputs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A video may always be next, while a product search comes later. Per-business targets preserve shopping supervision without feeding future purchase IDs into the current recommender.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.02684">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2604.02684-mbgr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f28720ce81a7ef92">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mbgr" data-paper-title="MBGR: Multi-Business Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-6183ac3f8450d70c">What does business-conditioned MoE share compared with training a separate generator for each business?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ambgr">MBGR: Multi-Business Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A shared expert pool learns common patterns, while business-conditioned gates produce specific representations and a conditioned autoencoder preserves SID semantics. Separate models duplicate learning but reduce conflict; shared models risk negative transfer. Genres proxy for businesses, not real cross-product labels. The local lack of gain should be retained.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Shopping and content may reuse one semantic expert at different weights. Separate models cannot exchange knowledge, but too much sharing can let high-traffic content suppress shopping.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.02684">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2604.02684-mbgr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6183ac3f8450d70c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mbgr" data-paper-title="MBGR: Multi-Business Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-3a0f76153c4a63db">Why not fill a missing future business event with padding or the last item in MBGR?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ambgr">MBGR: Multi-Business Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>There is no observed target for that business in the window. Filling it creates a false transition, so mask its loss. t′ must be the earliest position strictly after the current time with the right business identity, not merely a similar category. Training label availability differs from inference input visibility.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: If no purchase follows, the last movie is not a shopping positive. Masking preserves &#x27;unobserved&#x27; rather than inventing an answer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.02684">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2604.02684-mbgr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3a0f76153c4a63db">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onelatent" data-paper-title="OneLatent: Latent Reasoning for Efficient Foundation Recommendation Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-onelatent-08691361" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-7b09d92421cf94e0">Why supervise OneLatent with exploration, evaluation, and attribution instead of one fixed long chain of thought?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonelatent">OneLatent: Latent Reasoning for Efficient Foundation Recommendation Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The views cover discovery, comparison, and explanation; available perspectives per sample train a latent interface without a rigid template. It reduces explicit serving output, not proof of faithful reasoning recovery. Full-parameter training also contributes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: One example may have only a reliable evaluation, another all three views. They need not be forced into the same reasoning length.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 成本判断与本地边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30675v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../recommendation-components/2610.30675-onelatent/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7b09d92421cf94e0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onelatent" data-paper-title="OneLatent: Latent Reasoning for Efficient Foundation Recommendation Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-edb5f88714252428">Why can OneLatent&#x27;s latent tokens save online decoding without constituting a strict reasoning bottleneck?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonelatent">OneLatent: Latent Reasoning for Efficient Foundation Recommendation Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Training reconstructs exploration, evaluation, and attribution through latent tokens, then outputs semantic IDs instead of long reasons. Ordinary causal masks still expose original profile/history and all student weights update. Gains cannot be attributed to tokens alone storing every step. Local work reviewed evidence and cost without running a reproduction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A few internal markers can support a recommendation during training and only an ID appears online; faster output does not prove all reasoning is stored in markers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 成本判断与本地边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30675v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../recommendation-components/2610.30675-onelatent/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-edb5f88714252428">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onelatent" data-paper-title="OneLatent: Latent Reasoning for Efficient Foundation Recommendation Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ab91824a0488049a">Why is OneLatent&#x27;s interface not latent MSE distillation with an extra encoder/projector?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonelatent">OneLatent: Latent Reasoning for Efficient Foundation Recommendation Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>OneLatent trains all parameters of a causal student to reconstruct single- or multi-view reasons and predict SIDs, with no extra projector or strict bottleneck. MSE aligns feature coordinates, not generation. A fixture replacing the objective would be a new diagnostic; no such substitute was run locally.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Reconstructing reasons from markers supervises generatable content; shrinking Euclidean distance between vectors does not demonstrate that ability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 成本判断与本地边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30675v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../recommendation-components/2610.30675-onelatent/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ab91824a0488049a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onelatent" data-paper-title="OneLatent: Latent Reasoning for Efficient Foundation Recommendation Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-5ab3166d1802984b">Why average OneLatent reconstruction over each rationale&#x27;s tokens, then over available perspectives?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonelatent">OneLatent: Latent Reasoning for Efficient Foundation Recommendation Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Summation overweights long reasons and examples with more perspectives. Two-level averaging controls length and missingness. Teachers can read positives to create reasons, but the student prefix must exclude the target SID and positive description. Async serving caches and training costs are separate; local work is review-only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A 200-word rationale should not dominate a 20-word one by length alone, and a missing attribution view is not a real empty-text target.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 成本判断与本地边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30675v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../recommendation-components/2610.30675-onelatent/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5ab3166d1802984b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onemall" data-paper-title="OneMall: One Model, More Scenarios -- End-to-End Generative Recommender Family at Kuaishou E-Commerce" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-onemall-15aa9dcd" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-3318c79302b636b6">Why are shared item codes useful across OneMall cards, short videos, and livestreams?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonemall">OneMall: One Model, More Scenarios -- End-to-End Generative Recommender Family at Kuaishou E-Commerce</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Shared identity avoids fragmented mappings and separate modeling. Scene conditions and multi-behavior evidence distinguish consumption contexts. The code does not equalize exposure goals, video completion, commerce, or watch time, and transfer can conflict.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Jacket videos and cards share a code, but video completion and orders should not become equally strong positives.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.21770">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2601.21770-onemall/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3318c79302b636b6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onemall" data-paper-title="OneMall: One Model, More Scenarios -- End-to-End Generative Recommender Family at Kuaishou E-Commerce" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-361175a32963e5b8">Why does OneMall need scenario conditioning and multi-behavior cross-attention after unifying Semantic IDs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonemall">OneMall: One Model, More Scenarios -- End-to-End Generative Recommender Family at Kuaishou E-Commerce</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One output vocabulary gives each item one identity across scenes, not one behavior meaning. Scenario conditions specify the task and cross-attention selects pertinent history. Query-Former compression and sparse experts manage context and capacity. A unified model family still needs scene-specific behavior.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: The same jacket can be clicked in a card or ordered after a livestream. Its ID is shared, but live recommendation needs different behavior evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.21770">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2601.21770-onemall/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-361175a32963e5b8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onemall" data-paper-title="OneMall: One Model, More Scenarios -- End-to-End Generative Recommender Family at Kuaishou E-Commerce" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-5ad465e7480d6c89">How does OneMall&#x27;s sparse MoE change capacity and specialization relative to a dense generator?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonemall">OneMall: One Model, More Scenarios -- End-to-End Generative Recommender Family at Kuaishou E-Commerce</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Experts add conditional capacity while sparse activation limits per-request compute. Dense sharing is simpler but can favor frequent scenes. Experts can starve or duplicate, so total parameters are not effective capacity. Local SID and scene fusion do not reproduce full MoE/RL.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Live shopping and video can use different expert mixtures. If the gate always uses one expert, unused experts add no specialization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.21770">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2601.21770-onemall/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5ad465e7480d6c89">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onemall" data-paper-title="OneMall: One Model, More Scenarios -- End-to-End Generative Recommender Family at Kuaishou E-Commerce" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-aaf4db271080494e">Why don&#x27;t local three-level SIDs and a scene prompt prove OneMall Query-Former, MoE, and RL were reproduced?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonemall">OneMall: One Model, More Scenarios -- End-to-End Generative Recommender Family at Kuaishou E-Commerce</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The local path adds scene conditions, residual codes, and cross-behavior fusion. Query compression, actual routing, and policy updates need separate evidence. Report the small NDCG increase and Hit decrease within that scope rather than invoking the full paper family.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Three emitted item codes do not imply experts. Naming a loss &#x27;reward&#x27; does not establish RL without rollout and updates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.21770">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2601.21770-onemall/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-aaf4db271080494e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:oneranker" data-paper-title="OneRanker: Unified Generation and Ranking with One Model in Industrial Advertising Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-oneranker-399e9549" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-66bd49fd12f9b319">What prediction interfaces does OneRanker&#x27;s fake item token unify?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aoneranker">OneRanker: Unified Generation and Ranking with One Model in Industrial Advertising Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A shared representation conditions generation likelihood and value ranking, reducing objective separation. The token is an architectural placeholder, not a real item. Map outputs to a legal catalog and preserve each head&#x27;s objective.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: One candidate state answers likelihood and expected value, but the placeholder itself cannot be served as an ad.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.02999">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.02999-oneranker/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-66bd49fd12f9b319">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:oneranker" data-paper-title="OneRanker: Unified Generation and Ranking with One Model in Industrial Advertising Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-7e52b4a05d3de442">Why align OneRanker&#x27;s generation distribution and value head preferences?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aoneranker">OneRanker: Unified Generation and Ranking with One Model in Industrial Advertising Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Generation controls candidate availability and value controls ranking afterward. Reranking cannot recover valuable items the generator never produces. A shared fake-item token aligns interfaces and a consistency loss aligns distributions. Balance generation fit, value accuracy, and consistency to avoid suppressing useful differences.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: If generation favors cheap accessories while value prefers durable tools, reranking accessories cannot show tools. Consistency aims to give tools a generation chance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.02999">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.02999-oneranker/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7e52b4a05d3de442">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:oneranker" data-paper-title="OneRanker: Unified Generation and Ranking with One Model in Industrial Advertising Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-fddb820b8e41367d">What does generation consistency KL enforce beyond a shared backbone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aoneranker">OneRanker: Unified Generation and Ranking with One Model in Industrial Advertising Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Different heads can learn opposing preferences despite shared parameters. KL aligns distributions over identical candidates. This may reduce conflict or constrain useful specialization, so calibrate it. Agreement alone does not improve recommendation; both may prefer the wrong popular items.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A backbone does not stop accessory generation and tool value rankings from disagreeing. KL penalizes that disagreement, with direction still mattering.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.02999">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.02999-oneranker/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fddb820b8e41367d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:oneranker" data-paper-title="OneRanker: Unified Generation and Ranking with One Model in Industrial Advertising Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b88a0ca0f5a2a616">Why not subtract raw pgen and prank logits for OneRanker&#x27;s KL?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aoneranker">OneRanker: Unified Generation and Ranking with One Model in Industrial Advertising Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>KL compares normalized probabilities over aligned candidates and consistent temperatures. Mask padding and illegal candidates identically; do not expose value labels to generation. Fixed score mixing does not demonstrate learned distribution alignment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A constant logit shift leaves probabilities unchanged but changes squared differences. Full-catalog and ten-item normalizations cannot be treated as the same KL.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.02999">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.02999-oneranker/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b88a0ca0f5a2a616">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onerec" data-paper-title="OneRec: Unifying Retrieve and Rank with Generative Recommender and Iterative Preference Alignment" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-onerec-bec96f9e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-7150d36b246b8f85">Why concatenate multiple item SIDs into one autoregressive OneRec session target?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonerec">OneRec: Unifying Retrieve and Rank with Generative Recommender and Iterative Preference Alignment</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Later items can condition on earlier selections, unlike independent item generation. Hierarchical SIDs give composable addresses and reward evaluates the session. Order still matters, and diversity is not guaranteed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Follow a beginner photography tutorial with advanced practice instead of generating three independently relevant beginner videos.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.18965">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2502.18965-onerec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7150d36b246b8f85">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onerec" data-paper-title="OneRec: Unifying Retrieve and Rank with Generative Recommender and Iterative Preference Alignment" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-4d76f811142e31ca">Why train OneRec preference pairs from full current-policy sessions rather than individual items?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonerec">OneRec: Unifying Retrieve and Rank with Generative Recommender and Iterative Preference Alignment</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Session-level generation and reward can model coherence and diversity. Self-hard winner/loser pairs focus DPO on complete outputs the model confuses, comparing probability changes against a reference. Reward errors can steer updates incorrectly, and local results do not validate online gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Two five-video slates can be individually relevant but differ in repetition and flow. Session preferences teach which items work together.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.18965">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2502.18965-onerec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4d76f811142e31ca">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onerec" data-paper-title="OneRec: Unifying Retrieve and Rank with Generative Recommender and Iterative Preference Alignment" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-67abd43b2287aa84">Does OneRec self-hard DPO change the model or the search compared with widening the beam?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonerec">OneRec: Unifying Retrieve and Rank with Generative Recommender and Iterative Preference Alignment</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A wider beam explores the existing distribution; DPO updates policy probabilities using current-policy session pairs. Weak reward judging can hurt: local DPO loss fell quickly while NDCG went to zero. Preference fit does not establish ranking quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Search may find a good list, but training on the judge&#x27;s wrong winners can worsen future distributions despite a lower loss.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.18965">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2502.18965-onerec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-67abd43b2287aa84">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onerec" data-paper-title="OneRec: Unifying Retrieve and Rank with Generative Recommender and Iterative Preference Alignment" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a714ac3bdc5c99bd">Why don&#x27;t legal SID prefix constraints solve semantic-collision identity problems in OneRec?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonerec">OneRec: Unifying Retrieve and Rank with Generative Recommender and Iterative Preference Alignment</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A legal prefix proves catalog existence, not a unique item. Collisions require defined expansion or disambiguation, and uniqueness affects evaluation. Generate winners and losers from the current policy without gold injection. Legality, rewards, and ranking are separate checks; retain negative results.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Two films can share one legal code. Expanding to the correct film by reading the test label leaks the answer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.18965">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2502.18965-onerec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a714ac3bdc5c99bd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onerec-v2" data-paper-title="OneRec-V2 Technical Report" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-onerec-v2-8a1036e5" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-92affcd5baccf4bd">Why use real playback and negative feedback instead of an extra reward model in OneRec-V2?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonerec-v2">OneRec-V2 Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Direct behavior avoids reward-model training and error propagation. DARS adjusts duration opportunity and GBPO controls signed updates. Real behavior is still a biased satisfaction proxy. Removing a reward model does not remove calibration or constraints.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Long videos offer more watch seconds. Compare in user and duration buckets instead of treating all long watches as high satisfaction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.20900">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2508.20900-onerec-v2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-92affcd5baccf4bd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onerec-v2" data-paper-title="OneRec-V2 Technical Report" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-6a8c770978f6160d">Why supervise only the latest impression and share context K/V across OneRec-V2 decoder layers?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonerec-v2">OneRec-V2 Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Latest-impression supervision avoids full decoding for every history position. Context Processor produces one reusable K/V state and Lazy blocks read it to generate short SIDs. This reduces repeated history encoding and per-layer cache costs. Real-feedback alignment is separate and its effects cannot all be assigned to shared K/V.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: For three SID levels after a long history, each layer reads one shared memory rather than building its own full cache.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.20900">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2508.20900-onerec-v2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6a8c770978f6160d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onerec-v2" data-paper-title="OneRec-V2 Technical Report" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e475b3cbab1bb254">Why isn&#x27;t GBPO&#x27;s dynamic denominator equivalent to PPO clipping?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonerec-v2">OneRec-V2 Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>PPO clips the probability ratio; GBPO uses different stopped-gradient denominators by advantage sign. These limit updates differently. Replacing them with clipping loses defining behavior. Local feedback-weighted probability is not NDCG or online lift, and not all three seeds improved.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Positive and negative advantages respond differently as current probability changes; a symmetric clip does not establish equivalence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.20900">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2508.20900-onerec-v2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e475b3cbab1bb254">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onerec-v2" data-paper-title="OneRec-V2 Technical Report" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6ddf463c07f9e6ca">Why compute DARS quantiles within a user and duration bucket and detach GBPO denominators?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonerec-v2">OneRec-V2 Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Buckets compare similar viewing opportunities instead of mixing user habits and lengths. Stop-gradient prevents the denominator from adding unintended derivatives. Separate explicit dislike negatives from other zero advantages. Labels stay in post-training, not request inputs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Thirty seconds on a ten-second and ten-minute video are not directly comparable; differentiating through a numerically identical denominator changes the update.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.20900">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2508.20900-onerec-v2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6ddf463c07f9e6ca">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:oxygenrec-v2" data-paper-title="OxygenREC-v2: Internalizing Discrimination into Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-oxygenrec-v2-987866fe" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-bf86223c11e363a4">Why put click, cart, and order into OxygenREC-v2 decoder instructions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aoxygenrec-v2">OxygenREC-v2: Internalizing Discrimination into Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · JD.COM</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Goals change which candidates should be generated. Conditioning from the first SID can improve coverage before ranking, while weighted pretraining and post-training connect feedback. Use a legitimate task input, not one inferred from the test target. Local popularity is not real multibehavior supervision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Cart and casual click can need different first branches; reranking click-heavy candidates may miss order items.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24255">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.24255-oxygenrec-v2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bf86223c11e363a4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:oxygenrec-v2" data-paper-title="OxygenREC-v2: Internalizing Discrimination into Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-707ccd2ae0c3750c">Why condition OxygenREC-v2 from the first SID and select post-training constraints by uncertainty?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aoxygenrec-v2">OxygenREC-v2: Internalizing Discrimination into Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · JD.COM</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Late reranking cannot recover omitted items. A click/cart/order instruction shapes the whole decoding path. Training-only future behavior gives low-entropy positions confident teacher targets and high-entropy positions forward KL to preserve alternatives. Future events must not enter serving inputs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: An order instruction favors buyable branches from the start; uncertain branches retain several plausible products instead of one hard answer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24255">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.24255-oxygenrec-v2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-707ccd2ae0c3750c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:oxygenrec-v2" data-paper-title="OxygenREC-v2: Internalizing Discrimination into Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-5890fd364fd8b45e">Why is training with privileged future supervision different from serving with future features?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aoxygenrec-v2">OxygenREC-v2: Internalizing Discrimination into Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · JD.COM</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The training teacher can use later behavior to construct richer targets for a student that reads current inputs only. Future events are not yet available online. High-entropy forward KL constrains the distribution; it does not make future inputs legal.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A later lantern purchase can supervise a training example, but feeding it into the test prefix bypasses prediction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24255">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.24255-oxygenrec-v2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5890fd364fd8b45e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:oxygenrec-v2" data-paper-title="OxygenREC-v2: Internalizing Discrimination into Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-51c6f5f784b73056">Why marginalize the three proxy behaviors in local OxygenREC-v2 instead of selecting the held-out target&#x27;s class?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aoxygenrec-v2">OxygenREC-v2: Internalizing Discrimination into Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · JD.COM</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>MovieLens has no click/cart/order. Choosing a condition by the target&#x27;s popularity leaks identity clues. Marginalizing avoids that hint but changes the original task, so conclusions remain proxy-only. Verify privileged views, entropy routing, and losses separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Telling the model in advance the target is low-popularity narrows search; combine the unknown conditions without using the target.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24255">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.24255-oxygenrec-v2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-51c6f5f784b73056">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pinrec" data-paper-title="PinRec: Outcome-Conditioned, Multi-Token Generative Retrieval for Industry-Scale Recommendation Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-pinrec-66bf0193" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-98e4eb3523117a34">Why is PinRec desired outcome different from the next observed feedback label?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apinrec">PinRec: Outcome-Conditioned, Multi-Token Generative Retrieval for Industry-Scale Recommendation Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Desired outcome is a valid request condition. Future observed action is training supervision only; selecting conditions from test outcomes leaks information. Multi-vector windows represent several possible interests, not a guaranteed behavioral sequence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Request save-worthy candidates, but do not first check that the held-out item was saved and choose the condition accordingly.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.10507">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2504.10507-pinrec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-98e4eb3523117a34">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pinrec" data-paper-title="PinRec: Outcome-Conditioned, Multi-Token Generative Retrieval for Industry-Scale Recommendation Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-2ea183949a2f6b44">Why condition PinRec on desired outcomes and predict multiple item vectors for a future window?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apinrec">PinRec: Outcome-Conditioned, Multi-Token Generative Retrieval for Industry-Scale Recommendation Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One next-item target overrepresents common behavior and imposes a unique order. Desired outcomes guide heads, and multiple ANN-compatible vectors cover coexisting interests. Align predictions with window positives; do not treat duplicate popular vectors as distinct interests.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Set a save goal rather than casual browsing, and cover both gardening and baking from an unordered window.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.10507">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2504.10507-pinrec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2ea183949a2f6b44">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pinrec" data-paper-title="PinRec: Outcome-Conditioned, Multi-Token Generative Retrieval for Industry-Scale Recommendation Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-9ee1c6eb0e5343e2">Why are PinRec unordered-window retrieval and strict next-token hits different?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apinrec">PinRec: Outcome-Conditioned, Multi-Token Generative Retrieval for Industry-Scale Recommendation Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Multiple window positives allow alternative orders and coexisting interests. Strict next-item metrics accept only the immediately adjacent target. Align labels and pools for comparison; both local measures were negative and a looser metric should not hide that.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Retrieving a camera and tent fits the day window, but a tent does not count as the next item if the camera came first.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.10507">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2504.10507-pinrec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9ee1c6eb0e5343e2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pinrec" data-paper-title="PinRec: Outcome-Conditioned, Multi-Token Generative Retrieval for Industry-Scale Recommendation Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d2ba63933a870c32">Why normalize PinRec ANN outputs per head and deduplicate items?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apinrec">PinRec: Outcome-Conditioned, Multi-Token Generative Retrieval for Industry-Scale Recommendation Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Each vector must share index geometry and scale. Per-head normalization controls norms, and duplicate retrieved items need defined merging or deduplication. Match window target identities; repeating the same vector does not establish multi-interest learning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Three heads returning one popular camera cover one item; count unique hits and inspect whether heads differ.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.10507">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2504.10507-pinrec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d2ba63933a870c32">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:plum" data-paper-title="PLUM: Adapting Pre-trained Language Models for Industrial-scale Generative Recommendations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-plum-515f2ca7" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-099601afbacbb260">Why mix behavior and SID–metadata examples during PLUM CPT instead of only tuning next-item codes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aplum">PLUM: Adapting Pre-trained Language Models for Industrial-scale Generative Recommendations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind / YouTube</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Behavior teaches consumption transitions; text and ASR connect addresses to language semantics. CPT adapts pretrained knowledge to recommendation, then SFT focuses on retrieval. Mixture ratio matters, and lower loss need not improve search.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Learn both that a code means a camping tutorial and what users consume afterward.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.07784">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2510.07784-plum/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-099601afbacbb260">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:plum" data-paper-title="PLUM: Adapting Pre-trained Language Models for Industrial-scale Generative Recommendations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-0d1840f495739871">Why use hierarchical video SIDs and continue language pretraining in PLUM instead of enlarging an ID table?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aplum">PLUM: Adapting Pre-trained Language Models for Industrial-scale Generative Recommendations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind / YouTube</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Huge ID tables memorize items and share little with new ones. Composable SIDs and CPT connect behavior, text, ASR, and metadata to LM capacity before next-SID training. Beam search generates candidates online, but code quality still determines retrieval usefulness.</p>
