<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A new baking video can borrow a coarse baking code and distinguish itself at a fine level instead of learning an isolated ID from scarce clicks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.07784">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2510.07784-plum/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0d1840f495739871">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:plum" data-paper-title="PLUM: Adapting Pre-trained Language Models for Industrial-scale Generative Recommendations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1fb69e0e018a5cfa">Why cross random versus LM initialization with CPT on versus off in PLUM?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aplum">PLUM: Adapting Pre-trained Language Models for Industrial-scale Generative Recommendations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind / YouTube</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Four cells separate initialization, extra continued training, and their interaction. Locally CPT lowered loss without improving Recall and LM-initialized arms had zero hits. Convergence is not successful retrieval or general scaling evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Run random/no CPT, random/CPT, LM/no CPT, and LM/CPT to distinguish pretrained knowledge from extra training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.07784">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2510.07784-plum/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1fb69e0e018a5cfa">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:plum" data-paper-title="PLUM: Adapting Pre-trained Language Models for Industrial-scale Generative Recommendations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e504366a2a68836e">Why reconstruct the first r codeword layers in PLUM progressive masking instead of shuffling levels?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aplum">PLUM: Adapting Pre-trained Language Models for Industrial-scale Generative Recommendations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind / YouTube</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Residual levels accumulate coarse-to-fine meaning. Random prefix depths require each prefix to work; shuffling destroys that order. Mask SFT prompt loss, supervise only target SIDs, and use catalog trie legality. Training on prompt text changes the objective.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Sometimes reconstruct with coarse codes and sometimes add detail; using level three as the first code is not progressive reconstruction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.07784">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2510.07784-plum/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e504366a2a68836e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:promise" data-paper-title="PROMISE: Process Reward Models Unlock Test-Time Scaling Laws in Generative Recommendations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-promise-c348f413" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-e151a7faaadabf83">What does a SID prefix represent in PROMISE, and why does pruning remove many items?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apromise">PROMISE: Process Reward Models Unlock Test-Time Scaling Laws in Generative Recommendations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It is a hierarchical address prefix shared by a reachable subset of items. Descendants only refine that branch. Pruning can remove many unexplored items at once, so a bad process score can cause broad misses.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Pruning photography excludes all cameras, lenses, and accessories below it, including a perfectly relevant lens.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.04674">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2601.04674-promise/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e151a7faaadabf83">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:promise" data-paper-title="PROMISE: Process Reward Models Unlock Test-Time Scaling Laws in Generative Recommendations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-bd05a70bed64223d">Why reward intermediate SID paths in PROMISE rather than score only complete items?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apromise">PROMISE: Process Reward Models Unlock Test-Time Scaling Laws in Generative Recommendations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Early wrong semantic branches waste later computation. A lightweight process reward supplies dense training feedback and prunes drifting beams at inference. Wider beams can explore better paths but depend on reward quality and cost, not automatic improvement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Reject a home-decoration prefix early for a hiking request instead of waiting to generate a cushion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.04674">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2601.04674-promise/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bd05a70bed64223d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:promise" data-paper-title="PROMISE: Process Reward Models Unlock Test-Time Scaling Laws in Generative Recommendations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-f4c75f7ff9dd3eba">What extra judgment does PRM-guided beam widening add beyond likelihood?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apromise">PROMISE: Process Reward Models Unlock Test-Time Scaling Laws in Generative Recommendations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Likelihood prioritizes current model probability; PRM adds process value, allowing lower-likelihood but task-relevant paths. Scoring costs compute and can be biased. Test-time scaling is a budget–quality curve, not a guarantee.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: PRM can keep a less popular but correct branch; a popularity-biased PRM may still explore the wrong region.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.04674">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2601.04674-promise/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f4c75f7ff9dd3eba">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:promise" data-paper-title="PROMISE: Process Reward Models Unlock Test-Time Scaling Laws in Generative Recommendations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-93c178126616bf5a">Why define comparable scales across prefix lengths in PROMISE reward accumulation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apromise">PROMISE: Process Reward Models Unlock Test-Time Scaling Laws in Generative Recommendations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Long paths naturally sum more terms, potentially creating length bias. Compare beam candidates at consistent depths or with defined length handling, calibrate log-probability and λR, and retain legality, deduplication, and termination separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Three positive rewards are not inherently better than one if the paths have different depths. High PRM cannot legitimize an illegal item.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.04674">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2601.04674-promise/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-93c178126616bf5a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pushdualgen" data-paper-title="PushDualGen: Enabling LLMs to Generate Semantic IDs with Interpretable Copy for Industrial Push Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-pushdualgen-379bfcda" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-8086dc0e4ed1344b">Does a valid PushDualGen SID guarantee correct copy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apushdualgen">PushDualGen: Enabling LLMs to Generate Semantic IDs with Interpretable Copy for Industrial Push Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Catalog legality identifies a servable item. Copy also needs factual consistency, user evidence, and no exaggeration. Check identity and explanation quality independently.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Ordinary running shoes are a valid item, but claiming they are fireproof fails factual verification.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.07989">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.07989-pushdualgen/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8086dc0e4ed1344b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pushdualgen" data-paper-title="PushDualGen: Enabling LLMs to Generate Semantic IDs with Interpretable Copy for Industrial Push Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-2ef9c408f3412728">Why generate a servable SID before optionally generating explanation copy in PushDualGen?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apushdualgen">PushDualGen: Enabling LLMs to Generate Semantic IDs with Interpretable Copy for Industrial Push Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>SID identifies the recommendation and lets it enter serving immediately. A gate adds text only when needed, conditioned on that SID and history, saving decoding elsewhere. Fusion and consistency keep copy about the selected item; the recommendation remains usable without text.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A feed can return the item code alone, while a notification generates a reason about those running shoes, not an unrelated novel.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.07989">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.07989-pushdualgen/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2ef9c408f3412728">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pushdualgen" data-paper-title="PushDualGen: Enabling LLMs to Generate Semantic IDs with Interpretable Copy for Industrial Push Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-964d9882edb789a4">What budget and coverage trade-offs come from on-demand copy versus always generating explanations?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apushdualgen">PushDualGen: Enabling LLMs to Generate Semantic IDs with Interpretable Copy for Industrial Push Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Gating saves average decoding cost by reserving copy for useful scenarios, but some users may miss helpful explanations. Validate gating, caching, and scores for both modes. Do not present latency from one and effectiveness from the other as one path.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Report item-only feed speed separately from notification engagement with a generated sentence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.07989">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.07989-pushdualgen/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-964d9882edb789a4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pushdualgen" data-paper-title="PushDualGen: Enabling LLMs to Generate Semantic IDs with Interpretable Copy for Industrial Push Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-5368a0a2adb74791">Why define copy tensors and losses explicitly when PushDualGen has g=0?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apushdualgen">PushDualGen: Enabling LLMs to Generate Semantic IDs with Interpretable Copy for Industrial Push Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The skipped branch cannot require missing text; define masks and fallback states. At g=1, generate from the same SID and history. Placeholders are not explanations, and the local core scorer does not prove complete online copy generation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A zero vector can mark missing text, not justify decoding generic praise and claiming personalized consistency.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.07989">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.07989-pushdualgen/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5368a0a2adb74791">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:qgs" data-paper-title="From Item-Only to Query-Item: Query-Conditioned Generative Search with QGS in Quark" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-qgs-de75c3ea" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-3d9204e340d23d84">Why does QGS conditional probability describe a complete path rather than justify greedy per-step choices?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aqgs">From Item-Only to Query-Item: Query-Conditioned Generative Search with QGS in Quark</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China / Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>p(y|q,h) multiplies probabilities conditioned on prior generated tokens. Locally best choices need not maximize joint probability. Accumulate log probabilities under legal catalog paths. This identity alone does not establish the full search path in a local proxy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A slightly stronger first token may have weak legal continuations; another branch can win overall.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.25514">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.25514-qgs/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3d9204e340d23d84">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:qgs" data-paper-title="From Item-Only to Query-Item: Query-Conditioned Generative Search with QGS in Quark" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-9c44591d27ec4e42">Why serialize query and item together in QGS and still add feature interactions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aqgs">From Item-Only to Query-Item: Query-Conditioned Generative Search with QGS in Quark</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China / Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Joint serialization conditions generation on search query and history from the first item path, not just a general user vector. History encoding controls context cost and HFG-Attention adds sparse heterogeneous crosses. Its efficiency is architecture-specific, not proof every HSTU is linear.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: &#x27;Travel camera&#x27; and &#x27;indoor lighting&#x27; steer different paths; device and region interactions can further influence candidates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.25514">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.25514-qgs/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9c44591d27ec4e42">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:qgs" data-paper-title="From Item-Only to Query-Item: Query-Conditioned Generative Search with QGS in Quark" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e11df1e8a7b730ad">Why don&#x27;t Linear HSTU and ordinary HSTU have the same complexity just because they share a name?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aqgs">From Item-Only to Query-Item: Query-Conditioned Generative Search with QGS in Quark</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China / Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Linear forms need a specific kernel approximation or reordering. Standard SiLU(QKᵀ)V still has pairwise interactions, and HFG fusion adds separate costs. Do not invent kernel details absent from the source or omit dimensions and fields.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Removing softmax does not eliminate the N×N matrix; the actual rewrite or sparse execution matters.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.25514">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.25514-qgs/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e11df1e8a7b730ad">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:qgs" data-paper-title="From Item-Only to Query-Item: Query-Conditioned Generative Search with QGS in Quark" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-2af98e529550f6e3">Why doesn&#x27;t local QGS +0.73% NDCG validate full generation and a linear kernel?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aqgs">From Item-Only to Query-Item: Query-Conditioned Generative Search with QGS in Quark</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China / Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A shared scorer proxy changes rank scores without production queries or full kernel throughput measurements. Verify joint input, legal generation, field interaction, and attention separately. Hit declined and should also be reported.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A cross term on movie-transition scores can change NDCG without producing SID decoding traces.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.25514">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.25514-qgs/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2af98e529550f6e3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rag-generation" data-paper-title="Recommendation as Generation: Unifying Personalized Video Generation and Recommendation at Industrial Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-rag-generation-6f1ef070" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d0026c4f21594df2">Can RaG retrieval hits alone measure new video quality?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arag-generation">Recommendation as Generation: Unifying Personalized Video Generation and Recommendation at Industrial Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou / Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Retrieval evaluates existing candidates, while generated video requires visual, factual, and interest consistency. D-SID bridges interfaces, not success criteria. Local ranking cannot substitute for an unimplemented generator.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Correctly choosing camping can still yield physically impossible footage; pretty footage can also be irrelevant.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.25496">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2606.25496-rag-generation/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d0026c4f21594df2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rag-generation" data-paper-title="Recommendation as Generation: Unifying Personalized Video Generation and Recommendation at Industrial Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-151971fc5f0ff942">Why use disentangled SIDs to connect recommendation and generation in RaG?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arag-generation">Recommendation as Generation: Unifying Personalized Video Generation and Recommendation at Industrial Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou / Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Recommendation picks suitable content and generation controls creative attributes; entangling both can interfere. D-SIDs separate interfaces and cross-domain rewards coordinate what to recommend with how to produce it. The local discrete interface does not demonstrate video quality or full business lift.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A camping theme code supports selection while creative codes control shots or presentation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.25496">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2606.25496-rag-generation/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-151971fc5f0ff942">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rag-generation" data-paper-title="Recommendation as Generation: Unifying Personalized Video Generation and Recommendation at Industrial Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-14e25ecd90c38481">What does RaG cross-domain reward evaluate beyond visual generation quality?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arag-generation">Recommendation as Generation: Unifying Personalized Video Generation and Recommendation at Industrial Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou / Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It checks recommendation fit as well as visual quality and coordinates selection with creation. Rewards may conflict or lack verification. One proxy score cannot show both personalized relevance and actual visual gains. Locally only the D-SID interface ran.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Beautiful climbing footage can be irrelevant to easy camping, while matching a keyword does not prove watchable realistic video.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.25496">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2606.25496-rag-generation/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-14e25ecd90c38481">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rag-generation" data-paper-title="Recommendation as Generation: Unifying Personalized Video Generation and Recommendation at Industrial Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c98a66fe78f4cef1">What evidence would demonstrate full RaG video generation beyond the local D-SID interface?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arag-generation">Recommendation as Generation: Unifying Personalized Video Generation and Recommendation at Industrial Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou / Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Provide the real model and revision, conditions, generated videos, runnable training or inference commands, and quality evaluation. Discrete vectors and ranking metrics demonstrate transfer of code components, not execution. Paper online gains do not fill the local gap.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Returning two content/creative integers is a callable interface, not a video; a placeholder filename is not a visual artifact.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.25496">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2606.25496-rag-generation/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c98a66fe78f4cef1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rag-qac" data-paper-title="Unifying Ranking and Generation in Query Auto-Completion via Retrieval-Augmented Generation and Multi-Objective Alignment" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-rag-qac-5e006d24" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-09bb8a1517beab22">Why assess catalog groundedness separately from contextual groundedness in RAG-QAC?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arag-qac">Unifying Ranking and Generation in Query Auto-Completion via Retrieval-Augmented Generation and Multi-Objective Alignment</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Apple</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Catalog checks whether a suggestion maps to real searchable content; context checks fit with prefix and known needs. Each can pass alone and neither guarantees safety or engagement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Real adult hiking boots fail context for children&#x27;s rain boots, while an invented perfect child model fails the catalog.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.01023">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.01023-rag-qac/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-09bb8a1517beab22">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rag-qac" data-paper-title="Unifying Ranking and Generation in Query Auto-Completion via Retrieval-Augmented Generation and Multi-Objective Alignment" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d935bc68ea027e7f">Why retrieve a searchable catalog before multi-objective preference alignment in RAG-QAC?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arag-qac">Unifying Ranking and Generation in Query Auto-Completion via Retrieval-Augmented Generation and Multi-Objective Alignment</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Apple</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Free generation can create plausible suggestions with no results. Catalog retrieval grounds suggestions in traceable candidates, then SFT/DPO balance relevance, safety, engagement, context, and diversity. Alignment cannot create missing inventory, and engagement should not trump factuality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Retrieve real tents and cookware for &#x27;light camping&#x27; before suggesting a nonexistent model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.01023">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.01023-rag-qac/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d935bc68ea027e7f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rag-qac" data-paper-title="Unifying Ranking and Generation in Query Auto-Completion via Retrieval-Augmented Generation and Multi-Objective Alignment" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-7a913fd0cd8f5c0d">What do SFT and DPO add beyond a retrieval-template system for RAG-QAC?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arag-qac">Unifying Ranking and Generation in Query Auto-Completion via Retrieval-Augmented Generation and Multi-Objective Alignment</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Apple</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Templates ground some terms but fix expression and priorities. SFT learns contextual completions and DPO compares relevance, safety, engagement, and diversity. Goals can conflict; avoid losing truth for clicks. A fixed local scorer does not prove language post-training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Learn a trade-off between two searchable suggestions, one closer to the user and one covering a new direction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.01023">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.01023-rag-qac/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7a913fd0cd8f5c0d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rag-qac" data-paper-title="Unifying Ranking and Generation in Query Auto-Completion via Retrieval-Augmented Generation and Multi-Objective Alignment" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-5e959d9917f8d09a">Why keep RAG-QAC retrieval evidence separate from gold completion labels?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arag-qac">Unifying Ranking and Generation in Query Auto-Completion via Retrieval-Augmented Generation and Multi-Objective Alignment</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Apple</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Evidence comes from the prefix and catalog, while gold is training supervision. Retrieving from the correct held-out completion leaks it. Verify catalog and context independently rather than treating membership as all quality checks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Inserting the held-out tent model before generating lets the model repeat the answer rather than retrieve from the prefix.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.01023">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.01023-rag-qac/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5e959d9917f8d09a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rclrec" data-paper-title="RCLRec: Reverse Curriculum Learning for Modeling Sparse Conversions in Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">

<span id="paper-recommendation-rclrec-bd92f42c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-80bc5b5c19f75b0a">Does zero RCLRec curriculum quality stop the main objective from learning?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arclrec">RCLRec: Reverse Curriculum Learning for Modeling Sparse Conversions in Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International Digital Commerce Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Main loss plus λq(C) times the curriculum loss retains the main term at q(C)=0. Do not mask the whole sample. For gradient claims, distinguish whether the weight is trainable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A poor curriculum can be ignored while the true purchase label still trains the primary objective.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.28124">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.28124-rclrec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-80bc5b5c19f75b0a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rclrec" data-paper-title="RCLRec: Reverse Curriculum Learning for Modeling Sparse Conversions in Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-db3a9db18dacde46">Why put reversed conversion-related history into RCLRec&#x27;s decoder prefix and weight curriculum quality?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arclrec">RCLRec: Reverse Curriculum Learning for Modeling Sparse Conversions in Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International Digital Commerce Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Sparse conversion labels weakly supervise long histories. Selecting a related short subsequence and reversing it foregrounds events closer to conversion and creates intermediate supervision. Quality weighting limits weak curricula, but mistaken relevance can reinforce bias.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Start from cart addition and work back through comparison and search, while downweighting accidental browsing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.28124">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.28124-rclrec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-db3a9db18dacde46">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rclrec" data-paper-title="RCLRec: Reverse Curriculum Learning for Modeling Sparse Conversions in Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e5a302e159bb2001">How does quality weighting reduce uninformative curriculum supervision compared with equal weights?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arclrec">RCLRec: Reverse Curriculum Learning for Modeling Sparse Conversions in Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International Digital Commerce Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>q(C) limits irrelevant segments&#x27; influence on the main objective. It can be mistaken or overly concentrated and reduce coverage. Preserve the negative public proxy rather than assuming effectiveness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Ten unrelated clicks do not deserve more auxiliary weight than one clear compare-to-cart chain.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.28124">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.28124-rclrec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e5a302e159bb2001">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rclrec" data-paper-title="RCLRec: Reverse Curriculum Learning for Modeling Sparse Conversions in Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-86f07186e44d3ca0">Why preserve event timing and visibility when implementing reverse sequences in RCLRec?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arclrec">RCLRec: Reverse Curriculum Learning for Modeling Sparse Conversions in Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International Digital Commerce Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reversal changes prefix order, not what was observed before the target. Define selection, order, quality masks, and causal decoding for the transformed layout. Reversing a tensor with mismatched positions is not the specified curriculum.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Pre-purchase comparisons can be reversed, but a return after purchase cannot join the prefix.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
