<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:recgpt-v3" data-paper-title="RecGPT-V3 Technical Report" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-recgpt-v3-d1c7b19e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-506207a0481453a7">Why store original behavior references and timestamps in a RecGPT-V3 memory unit?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arecgpt-v3">RecGPT-V3 Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Provenance enables evidence tracing and incremental updates instead of letting summaries drift. Only relevant units change, but traceability is not lossless or causal correctness. Refresh and expiry still matter.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Link &#x27;planning to camp&#x27; to dated browsing records so the right unit can be updated when needs change.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.15591">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.15591-recgpt-v3/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-506207a0481453a7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:recgpt-v3" data-paper-title="RecGPT-V3 Technical Report" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-7fce71e69a1528f4">Why change memory, item interface, and reasoning representation together in RecGPT-V3?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arecgpt-v3">RecGPT-V3 Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>CoT compression alone leaves repeated history reads and losses mapping natural language to items. Memory Hub updates traceable units incrementally, SID connects to products, and latent tokens cut reasoning output. They address different costs, while production ranking feedback also contributes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Update only the photography memory after a camera view, emit an item code, and use shorter latent reasoning. Text length alone misses the other savings.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.15591">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.15591-recgpt-v3/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7fce71e69a1528f4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:recgpt-v3" data-paper-title="RecGPT-V3 Technical Report" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-f3e873b9a1426179">What training protection does latent internalization add beyond deleting explicit CoT?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arecgpt-v3">RecGPT-V3 Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Segment, cross-segment, and full-chain reconstruction transfer teacher information into latent slots. Removing output alone only saves text. Reconstruction does not prove faithful reasoning, and teacher quality and freezing matter. Local synchronous drift failed before teacher warm-up and freezing improved results.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Teaching four slots to support prior explanations differs from not printing an explanation; moving teacher and student together can destabilize targets.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.15591">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.15591-recgpt-v3/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f3e873b9a1426179">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:recgpt-v3" data-paper-title="RecGPT-V3 Technical Report" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-04acbce36f43f346">Why report RecGPT-V3 selection history and head share with final local metrics?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arecgpt-v3">RecGPT-V3 Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Teacher warm-up and freezing were selected through iterations; the final single seed is not preregistered stability evidence. Rising head share can signal a popularity shortcut. Counts of memory and latent tokens are structural, not latency or 14B measurements.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Reducing 40 events to 14 inputs changes budget but does not promise a 65% speedup.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.15591">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.15591-recgpt-v3/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-04acbce36f43f346">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:reward-guided-decoding" data-paper-title="Reward Guided Decoding for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-reward-guided-decoding-a3100a32" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-5f4bd9838c190a35">Can reward-guided decoding give positive mass to a sequence with P0=0?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Areward-guided-decoding">Reward Guided Decoding for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Information Engineering, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Not under the closed form. Multiplying strict zero by an exponential stays zero, and normalization does not create support. Smoothing, candidate expansion, or generator changes are separate steps.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A movie absent from all legal candidates cannot be recovered by assigning a high novelty reward.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25344">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.25344-reward-guided-decoding/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5f4bd9838c190a35">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:reward-guided-decoding" data-paper-title="Reward Guided Decoding for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-0710a847a39d981a">Why does exponential reward-guided decoding preserve a prior while depending on KL temperature?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Areward-guided-decoding">Reward Guided Decoding for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Information Engineering, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The tilted distribution multiplies prior probability by exponentiated reward. Smaller temperature follows reward more aggressively; larger approaches the prior. Search and normalization affect approximation, and reward errors can hurt even without training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Moderate novelty can elevate relevant niche movies; too low a temperature can select irrelevant novelties.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25344">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.25344-reward-guided-decoding/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0710a847a39d981a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:reward-guided-decoding" data-paper-title="Reward Guided Decoding for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-94cf388dc09984d0">When does exponential tilting correspond to adding logits, and when does it not?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Areward-guided-decoding">Reward Guided Decoding for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Information Engineering, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>On identical support, log Q equals log P0+R/β up to a shared normalizer. Adding reward to raw P0 instead changes the distribution. Candidate truncation also changes support and normalization and is not the exact closed form.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Adding one to probabilities 0.9 and 0.1 has a different effect from adding it in log space.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25344">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.25344-reward-guided-decoding/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-94cf388dc09984d0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:reward-guided-decoding" data-paper-title="Reward Guided Decoding for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-13edd1a09ebb9259">Why implement reward tilting with logsumexp and test temperature limits?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Areward-guided-decoding">Reward Guided Decoding for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Information Engineering, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Raw exponentials overflow. Normalize in log space; large β should approach the prior, small β emphasize reward, and illegal entries stay masked. Separate truncated approximation from exact normalization. Local novelty reward reduced NDCG, so higher reward did not establish better ranking.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: exp(1000) can overflow; stable normalization fixes numerics, not irrelevant novelty at low temperature.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25344">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.25344-reward-guided-decoding/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-13edd1a09ebb9259">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rgalign-rec" data-paper-title="RGAlign-Rec: Ranking-Guided Alignment for Latent Query Reasoning in Recommendation Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-rgalign-rec-56b59d1c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-bdd19e3b729ffb62">Is an RGAlign-Rec latent query an actual search term typed by the user?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Argalign-rec">RGAlign-Rec: Ranking-Guided Alignment for Latent Query Reasoning in Recommendation Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Forth AI / Shopee / Singapore University of Technology and Design</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It is verbalized intent generated from user context to connect item retrieval with ranking needs. Fluent text does not establish that the user said it. Distinguish observed behavior from inferred intent to understand the supervision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>After a user views camping content, the model may infer “lightweight tent” even if no such search appears in the log.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12968">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.12968-rgalign-rec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bdd19e3b729ffb62">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rgalign-rec" data-paper-title="RGAlign-Rec: Ranking-Guided Alignment for Latent Query Reasoning in Recommendation Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-6398abbf95278d4e">Why does RGAlign use the ranker&#x27;s item preferences to choose query winners and losers?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Argalign-rec">RGAlign-Rec: Ranking-Guided Alignment for Latent Query Reasoning in Recommendation Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Forth AI / Shopee / Singapore University of Technology and Design</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A fluent latent query can miss items the ranker values. Generate alternatives, rank the items they retrieve, and derive demonstrations and preference pairs to align query generation with top-ranked retrieval. RG-SFT learns the mapping and DPO strengthens relative preferences. Supervision still inherits the ranker&#x27;s judgment, not independent satisfaction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>History may suggest beginner photography or professional lenses. If ranking favors a lightweight beginner camera, prefer the first query rather than the one phrased most naturally.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12968">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.12968-rgalign-rec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6398abbf95278d4e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rgalign-rec" data-paper-title="RGAlign-Rec: Ranking-Guided Alignment for Latent Query Reasoning in Recommendation Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-18b3599a62f2f2ae">How does ranking-guided query alignment differ from ordinary language SFT?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Argalign-rec">RGAlign-Rec: Ranking-Guided Alignment for Latent Query Reasoning in Recommendation Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Forth AI / Shopee / Singapore University of Technology and Design</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>SFT maximizes demonstration text likelihood. Ranking guidance constructs preferred and rejected queries from downstream item preferences, tying verbalized intent to ranking. Ranker preferences can be biased and are not causal user ground truth.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A fancier query may retrieve worse candidates; downstream feedback can distinguish the two.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12968">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.12968-rgalign-rec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-18b3599a62f2f2ae">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rgalign-rec" data-paper-title="RGAlign-Rec: Ranking-Guided Alignment for Latent Query Reasoning in Recommendation Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a57676e168ae136a">How should we distinguish local RGAlign queries from the production LLM pipeline?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Argalign-rec">RGAlign-Rec: Ranking-Guided Alignment for Latent Query Reasoning in Recommendation Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Forth AI / Shopee / Singapore University of Technology and Design</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A fixed public MovieLens candidate protocol checks the ranking-guided core, not private features, the production base, or traffic. Compare positive and negative queries under the same context and candidates. Do not choose winners with test labels.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Better offline candidate scores do not establish higher live conversion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12968">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.12968-rgalign-rec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a57676e168ae136a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rolegen" data-paper-title="Awakening Dormant Users: Generative Recommendation with Counterfactual Functional Role Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-rolegen-9ce78677" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-5116f7e1f78cdcad">Does “role” in RoleGen mean a user identity or an item&#x27;s function along a conversion path?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arolegen">Awakening Dormant Users: Generative Recommendation with Counterfactual Functional Role Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It means an item&#x27;s function in the conversion path, not a user occupation or demographic. An LLM Reasoner infers item roles and passes candidates to the SID generator and feedback loop. The roles are model interpretations, not observed causal identities.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An item can help comparison in one trajectory and be the purchase in another, regardless of whether the user is a student.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.13134">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.13134-rolegen/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5116f7e1f78cdcad">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rolegen" data-paper-title="Awakening Dormant Users: Generative Recommendation with Counterfactual Functional Role Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c0450005c9756e63">Why does RoleGen infer conversion-path functions rather than rely on similarity to reactivate dormant users?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arolegen">Awakening Dormant Users: Generative Recommendation with Counterfactual Functional Role Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>For inactive users, repeatedly serving similar old items can narrow interests. Functional roles model exploration, comparison, and conversion. Counterfactual paths estimate an item&#x27;s instrumental contribution, which feeds the SID generator and iterative reflection. These estimates rely on model and data assumptions, not causality identified by observed trajectories alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A camera buyer may have watched reviews and photography tutorials. A tutorial is not similar to a camera listing but may reactivate interest.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.13134">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.13134-rolegen/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c0450005c9756e63">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rolegen" data-paper-title="Awakening Dormant Users: Generative Recommendation with Counterfactual Functional Role Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-56695ae911654777">How does counterfactual instrumental contribution differ from co-occurrence similarity?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arolegen">Awakening Dormant Users: Generative Recommendation with Counterfactual Functional Role Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Co-occurrence describes what appears together. Instrumentality asks how an outcome might change if the item were removed. A local proxy and do notation do not identify real causal effects.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Phones and chargers may be bought together without charger recommendations causing phone purchases.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.13134">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.13134-rolegen/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-56695ae911654777">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rolegen" data-paper-title="Awakening Dormant Users: Generative Recommendation with Counterfactual Functional Role Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-3de78a17bbd52912">Can RoleGen&#x27;s local public data establish production conversion among dormant users?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arolegen">Awakening Dormant Users: Generative Recommendation with Counterfactual Functional Role Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. A MovieLens subset and proxy objective check the core path, without private dormant-user logs or actual traffic buckets. Log score provenance, candidates, and feedback. Do not present proxy deltas as live intervention effects.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A movie preference ranking change is not causal lift in e-commerce conversion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.13134">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.13134-rolegen/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3de78a17bbd52912">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:s-grec" data-paper-title="S-GRec: Personalized Semantic-Aware Generative Recommendation with Asymmetric Advantage" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-s-grec-c5ba1bc0" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-2108822c2ae03b8d">Why keep the large judge off S-GRec&#x27;s online generation path?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3As-grec">S-GRec: Personalized Semantic-Aware Generative Recommendation with Asymmetric Advantage</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent / WeChat Channels</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Offline judging supplies per-aspect preferences; a lightweight generator emits SIDs without online LLM latency. Judge quality still depends on training data and is not cost-free.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An expensive teacher trains semantic preference while a small model serves.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.10606">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.10606-s-grec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2108822c2ae03b8d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:s-grec" data-paper-title="S-GRec: Personalized Semantic-Aware Generative Recommendation with Asymmetric Advantage" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-ef678d9523c7b0d4">Why add bounded semantic advantage only when it agrees with business advantage?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3As-grec">S-GRec: Personalized Semantic-Aware Generative Recommendation with Asymmetric Advantage</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent / WeChat Channels</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The rewards have different scales. A2PO standardizes each within rollout groups, anchors to business advantage, and adds semantic signal only with matching sign and bounded magnitude. This does not remove reward bias.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A pleasing rationale cannot turn negative business feedback positive.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.10606">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.10606-s-grec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ef678d9523c7b0d4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:s-grec" data-paper-title="S-GRec: Personalized Semantic-Aware Generative Recommendation with Asymmetric Advantage" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-8b5a787178e7a276">How do user-conditioned aspect weights differ from one fixed vector?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3As-grec">S-GRec: Personalized Semantic-Aware Generative Recommendation with Asymmetric Advantage</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent / WeChat Channels</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The judge supplies aspect scores and an aggregator gives normalized nonnegative per-user weights. Fixed weights express one trade-off; conditional weights personalize the same content but do not prove satisfaction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One user prioritizes history fit while another prioritizes novelty.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.10606">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.10606-s-grec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8b5a787178e7a276">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:s-grec" data-paper-title="S-GRec: Personalized Semantic-Aware Generative Recommendation with Asymmetric Advantage" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-1e67157c01accb0b">Is local S-GRec business reward real eCPM?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3As-grec">S-GRec: Personalized Semantic-Aware Generative Recommendation with Asymmetric Advantage</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent / WeChat Channels</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Public data lacks money signals; it uses next-item ranking. Judge, generation, and policy run at reduced scale with different labels.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A correct next movie is behavioral evidence, not ad revenue.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.10606">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.10606-s-grec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1e67157c01accb0b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:s2gr" data-paper-title="S2GR: Stepwise Semantic-Guided Reasoning in Latent Space for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-s2gr-c72e2aca" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-870e580deebf4aef">Is S2GR&#x27;s thinking token a long free-form natural-language chain?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3As2gr">S2GR: Stepwise Semantic-Guided Reasoning in Latent Space for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It is an intermediate state before each SID level, aligned to that level&#x27;s codebook. SIDs remain a discrete hierarchical path; the name does not prove natural-language reasoning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Insert a state, choose a level code, and move on without emitting a prose essay.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.18664">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2601.18664-s2gr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-870e580deebf4aef">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:s2gr" data-paper-title="S2GR: Stepwise Semantic-Guided Reasoning in Latent Space for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-833b7b1f56656208">Why insert a thinking token before each SID stage and align it to codebooks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3As2gr">S2GR: Stepwise Semantic-Guided Reasoning in Latent Space for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Early coarse codes constrain later paths. Intermediate states receive contrastive codebook supervision; collaborative graphs and balancing add behavior and usage signals. This need not be faithful natural-language reasoning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Align the intermediate outdoor-category state before selecting finer camping gear codes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.18664">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2601.18664-s2gr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-833b7b1f56656208">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:s2gr" data-paper-title="S2GR: Stepwise Semantic-Guided Reasoning in Latent Space for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-30fd271baa0367d3">What do thinking alignment and codebook load balancing constrain?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3As2gr">S2GR: Stepwise Semantic-Guided Reasoning in Latent Space for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Alignment links intermediate states to code semantics. Load balancing prevents concentrated code use. Uniform use does not establish semantics, and semantic alignment does not ensure balance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Randomly spreading examples can fix utilization while losing meaning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.18664">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2601.18664-s2gr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-30fd271baa0367d3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:s2gr" data-paper-title="S2GR: Stepwise Semantic-Guided Reasoning in Latent Space for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-ee90eadef5b0ee26">Are the local S2GR codebook and thinking states the production model?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3As2gr">S2GR: Stepwise Semantic-Guided Reasoning in Latent Space for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Fixed MovieLens data tests core mechanisms. Align current code, earlier codes, and thinking position; never tune balance using test catalog labels. Production gains are author-reported.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Uniform use in a small catalog does not validate a production hierarchy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.18664">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2601.18664-s2gr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ee90eadef5b0ee26">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sessionrec" data-paper-title="SessionRec: Next Session Prediction Paradigm For Generative Sequential Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-sessionrec-2fd19641" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-1fad52275cdd3908">Is SessionRec&#x27;s session token one item or a visit representation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asessionrec">SessionRec: Next Session Prediction Paradigm For Generative Sequential Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>ISE aggregates multiple items into one visit representation; SSE models transitions across visits. The next visit can include several positives.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Group A/B/C into one visit and target D/E together.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.10157">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2502.10157-sessionrec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1fad52275cdd3908">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sessionrec" data-paper-title="SessionRec: Next Session Prediction Paradigm For Generative Sequential Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-9400ea46fb6842b9">Why aggregate sessions before predicting multiple next-session positives?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asessionrec">SessionRec: Next Session Prediction Paradigm For Generative Sequential Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Items within a visit often share intent rather than a unique order. ISE aggregates; SSE learns cross-visit transitions. Supervise all next-session positives and use actual skipped impressions. Bad session boundaries can mix intents.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Group tent, bag, and mat as one shopping visit before predicting the next hiking visit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.10157">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2502.10157-sessionrec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9400ea46fb6842b9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sessionrec" data-paper-title="SessionRec: Next Session Prediction Paradigm For Generative Sequential Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-3e0685c171309fa7">Which ordering do ISE and SSE handle?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asessionrec">SessionRec: Next Session Prediction Paradigm For Generative Sequential Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>ISE aggregates items within a visit, and SSE models chronological visit transitions. Mean ISE downplays within-visit order, not all order. SSE can use Transformer or HSTU.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Noon versus evening visits matter even if within-visit browse ordering is weak.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.10157">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2502.10157-sessionrec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3e0685c171309fa7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sessionrec" data-paper-title="SessionRec: Next Session Prediction Paradigm For Generative Sequential Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-8fa08745cf9658a9">Can random catalog negatives be labeled skipped exposures?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asessionrec">SessionRec: Next Session Prediction Paradigm For Generative Sequential Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Hard negatives are actual exposed but unclicked items in that visit. Training samples a positive per round for CE, while evaluation keeps the full positive set.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An unseen movie is not a rejected impression.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.10157">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2502.10157-sessionrec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8fa08745cf9658a9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sigma" data-paper-title="SIGMA: A Semantic-Grounded Instruction-Driven Generative Multi-Task Recommender at AliExpress" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-sigma-3e17a33a" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-354f3ed585098924">Why combine a short SID prefix with unique item identity?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asigma">SIGMA: A Semantic-Grounded Instruction-Driven Generative Multi-Task Recommender at AliExpress</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / AliExpress</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The prefix narrows search; unique item representations retain exact identity inside its subcatalog. It is a middle ground between long SID generation and full-catalog ANN.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Choose a sneaker subcatalog, then distinguish exact models.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.22913">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.22913-sigma/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-354f3ed585098924">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sigma" data-paper-title="SIGMA: A Semantic-Grounded Instruction-Driven Generative Multi-Task Recommender at AliExpress" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1ed6d59e347fea5a">Why use short SID prefixes and unique IDs instead of all-SID generation or global ANN?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asigma">SIGMA: A Semantic-Grounded Instruction-Driven Generative Multi-Task Recommender at AliExpress</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / AliExpress</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Prefix generation locates a semantic catalog; unique IDs disambiguate items and local ANN limits cost. Multiview alignment connects semantics and behavior; APF trades precision and diversity with confidence. Missed prefixes constrain recall.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Search within outdoor equipment; if only home goods was generated, local ANN cannot find tents.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.22913">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.22913-sigma/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1ed6d59e347fea5a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sigma" data-paper-title="SIGMA: A Semantic-Grounded Instruction-Driven Generative Multi-Task Recommender at AliExpress" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-87385cdc98e69544">How do multitask instructions differ from next-item-only training?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asigma">SIGMA: A Semantic-Grounded Instruction-Driven Generative Multi-Task Recommender at AliExpress</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / AliExpress</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Instructions specify query, long-tail, discovery, and other goals. Evidence of following them requires task data and evaluation; prompting alone does not teach seasonality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The same history can request novelty or a familiar category.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.22913">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.22913-sigma/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-87385cdc98e69544">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sigma" data-paper-title="SIGMA: A Semantic-Grounded Instruction-Driven Generative Multi-Task Recommender at AliExpress" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a12be252b249dff8">Does exact local cosine top-k establish production ANN latency?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asigma">SIGMA: A Semantic-Grounded Instruction-Driven Generative Multi-Task Recommender at AliExpress</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / AliExpress</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It verifies retrieval logic on a small catalog with proxy tasks. It does not measure large-scale index speed or establish APF/online uplift.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Scanning thousands of items differs from billion-item service.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.22913">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.22913-sigma/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a12be252b249dff8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:snaplgr" data-paper-title="LLM-Based Generative Retrieval for Snapchat Content Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-snaplgr-28d916e6" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-86180448fcf71ebd">Why build a co-engagement graph before SnapLGR SIDs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asnaplgr">LLM-Based Generative Retrieval for Snapchat Content Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Snap Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Propagation adds collaborative relationships, residual quantization turns them into hierarchical paths, and generation predicts codes from history. Behavior complements content.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Visually different items consumed by one audience can become connected.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28895">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.28895-snaplgr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-86180448fcf71ebd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:snaplgr" data-paper-title="LLM-Based Generative Retrieval for Snapchat Content Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-e972912a0c70610f">Why propagate co-engagement, quantize, then ground generated tokens?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asnaplgr">LLM-Based Generative Retrieval for Snapchat Content Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Snap Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Graphs add collaborative signals, quantization encodes them in discrete paths, grounding ties codes back to content, and next-SID prediction learns transitions. Popularity bias can propagate too.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Visually different co-consumed items can become neighbors, but codes still must resolve reliably to relevant content.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28895">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.28895-snaplgr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e972912a0c70610f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:snaplgr" data-paper-title="LLM-Based Generative Retrieval for Snapchat Content Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-42f47c26b383eb22">What does grounding SID tokens add beyond discrete-code likelihood?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asnaplgr">LLM-Based Generative Retrieval for Snapchat Content Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Snap Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Alignment preserves content meaning instead of learning only code transitions. Its benefit depends on embedding and graph quality, not any arbitrary semantic code.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Related videos&#x27; code representations should reflect their content relationship.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28895">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.28895-snaplgr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-42f47c26b383eb22">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:snaplgr" data-paper-title="LLM-Based Generative Retrieval for Snapchat Content Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6a48591353777092">What behavior can graph propagation and quantization use?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asnaplgr">LLM-Based Generative Retrieval for Snapchat Content Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Snap Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Only allowed training co-engagement, without future test edges. Pin codebook and mapping versions. Public features do not reproduce Snap logs, scale, or traffic.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Test clicks in the graph leak retrieval relationships.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28895">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.28895-snaplgr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6a48591353777092">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sona" data-paper-title="Sona Technical Report" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-sona-74c5ab5b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-db84c085c9995808">Why use both SID generation and ranking in Sona?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asona">Sona Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Yandex</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Share user state across candidate generation and fine ranking instead of duplicating representations. A large teacher guides training only; one model serves.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Generate songs and score specific songs from the same user state.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.11015">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.11015-sona/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-db84c085c9995808">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sona" data-paper-title="Sona Technical Report" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d656f31a07458ede">Why share user state between Sona generation and ranking, with teacher only in training?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asona">Sona Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Yandex</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Separate models repeat history encoding and can learn inconsistent representations. One chronological compressed state supports joint generation and ranking, with training-only teacher supervision. It does not eliminate missed retrieval or compression loss; retain local negative results.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Both paths respond to a shift from rock to classical without calling a large teacher online.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.11015">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.11015-sona/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d656f31a07458ede">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sona" data-paper-title="Sona Technical Report" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-f12020c85502e7d7">How does a unified model differ from deleting an intermediate ranker?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asona">Sona Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Yandex</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Joint generation, ranking, and distillation must replace functionality and handle long history. Compare coverage and robustness; fewer models alone do not prove improvement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Dropping pre-ranking without joint training can just remove functionality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.11015">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.11015-sona/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f12020c85502e7d7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sona" data-paper-title="Sona Technical Report" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d8da9beed55e2ba5">Does Sona call its teacher at serving?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asona">Sona Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Yandex</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Teacher is training-only. Local work omits the full teacher, music tokenizer, and 15-plus-source production stack. Generation/ranking losses share state with distinct masks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Calling the large teacher online changes the cost contract.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.11015">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.11015-sona/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d8da9beed55e2ba5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:spar-prefix-balance" data-paper-title="SPAR: Stepwise Personalized Autoregressive Recommendation with Prefix-Balanced Semantic IDs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-spar-prefix-balance-335a990d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c23aad85b0e6ef99">Why repair SPAR load within each parent SID prefix?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aspar-prefix-balance">SPAR: Stepwise Personalized Autoregressive Recommendation with Prefix-Balanced Semantic IDs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Electronic Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Compare sibling load by interaction weight, not item count, while freezing centers and preserving hierarchical semantics through low-distortion moves.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two branches with ten items each may have very different traffic.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.27898v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../recommendation-components/2610.27898-spar-prefix-balance/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c23aad85b0e6ef99">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:spar-prefix-balance" data-paper-title="SPAR: Stepwise Personalized Autoregressive Recommendation with Prefix-Balanced Semantic IDs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-e5b3653237f86b16">Why freeze centers and use a load bound accounting for the heaviest item?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aspar-prefix-balance">SPAR: Stepwise Personalized Autoregressive Recommendation with Prefix-Balanced Semantic IDs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Electronic Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixing centers and parents limits semantic drift. Indivisible weights can make exact averages infeasible; move at most once per item and choose low-cost feasible destinations. Local scope excludes retrieval and preference alignment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Total load 12 across three branches cannot be exactly four each if one item weighs six.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.27898v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../recommendation-components/2610.27898-spar-prefix-balance/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e5b3653237f86b16">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:spar-prefix-balance" data-paper-title="SPAR: Stepwise Personalized Autoregressive Recommendation with Prefix-Balanced Semantic IDs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1bf28639da1e480d">How do feasible RQ-PIB moves differ from global equal buckets?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aspar-prefix-balance">SPAR: Stepwise Personalized Autoregressive Recommendation with Prefix-Balanced Semantic IDs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Electronic Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Choose a currently feasible low-distortion move under load limits and indivisible-item weights. It guarantees neither exact equality nor global optimum.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A very popular item cannot be split across branches merely to equalize loads.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.27898v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../recommendation-components/2610.27898-spar-prefix-balance/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1bf28639da1e480d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:spar-prefix-balance" data-paper-title="SPAR: Stepwise Personalized Autoregressive Recommendation with Prefix-Balanced Semantic IDs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-148a33689a91e77f">Does local SPAR implement PATH retrieval and full SFT+DPO?</h2>
