<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aspar-prefix-balance">SPAR: Stepwise Personalized Autoregressive Recommendation with Prefix-Balanced Semantic IDs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Electronic Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It implements post-freeze RQ-PIB only. Skip zero-load groups, move items at most once, and keep parents and centers fixed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Local branch balancing does not train prefix personalization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.27898v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../recommendation-components/2610.27898-spar-prefix-balance/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-148a33689a91e77f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:static-constraint-decoding" data-paper-title="Vectorizing the Trie: Efficient Constrained Decoding for LLM-based Generative Retrieval on Accelerators" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-static-constraint-decoding-c02cbeaf" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-e0d73a2f68dae433">Why compile legal item tries into device-side transitions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Astatic-constraint-decoding">Vectorizing the Trie: Efficient Constrained Decoding for LLM-based Generative Retrieval on Accelerators</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Inventory/geography constraints need legal decoding, but CPU pointer traversals cause round trips. CSR and shallow dense lookup provide contiguous token and destination indices on accelerators.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Gather legal successors from one row rather than walking a CPU trie.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.22647">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../recommendation-components/2602.22647-static-constraint-decoding/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e0d73a2f68dae433">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:static-constraint-decoding" data-paper-title="Vectorizing the Trie: Efficient Constrained Decoding for LLM-based Generative Retrieval on Accelerators" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-9de99ca7ecd033e3">Why use full-vocabulary log-softmax before masking?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Astatic-constraint-decoding">Vectorizing the Trie: Efficient Constrained Decoding for LLM-based Generative Retrieval on Accelerators</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Constraints remove invalid paths, not alter original conditional probabilities. Legal-set renormalization favors some small sets in cross-beam comparison. CSR accelerates lookup; synchronize prefixes and states.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A lone legal child should not become probability one and unfairly beat a better-supported path.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.22647">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../recommendation-components/2602.22647-static-constraint-decoding/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9de99ca7ecd033e3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:static-constraint-decoding" data-paper-title="Vectorizing the Trie: Efficient Constrained Decoding for LLM-based Generative Retrieval on Accelerators" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-94874bbc3ffd8e6f">How does legal-only softmax differ from full log-softmax then masking?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Astatic-constraint-decoding">Vectorizing the Trie: Efficient Constrained Decoding for LLM-based Generative Retrieval on Accelerators</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Legal renormalization changes prefix score scales according to set size. Full log-softmax preserves model probabilities while excluding invalid tokens.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A parent with one legal successor gets an artificial boost if renormalized alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.22647">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../recommendation-components/2602.22647-static-constraint-decoding/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-94874bbc3ffd8e6f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:static-constraint-decoding" data-paper-title="Vectorizing the Trie: Efficient Constrained Decoding for LLM-based Generative Retrieval on Accelerators" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-622b5fbde0e5eba1">Why reorder prefix and trie node together after beam selection?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Astatic-constraint-decoding">Vectorizing the Trie: Efficient Constrained Decoding for LLM-based Generative Retrieval on Accelerators</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Prefix and legal state are paired. Children can come from different parents; mismatching states applies the wrong mask. Pin trie versions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A clothing prefix cannot keep a food node for next-step legality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.22647">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../recommendation-components/2602.22647-static-constraint-decoding/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-622b5fbde0e5eba1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tagr" data-paper-title="TAGR: Temporally Adaptive Generative Recommendation for Industrial Live-Streaming Advertising" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-tagr-4f20f91f" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-566653d184f1fc06">Why combine LSID, IAG, and IOPO adaptation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atagr">TAGR: Temporally Adaptive Generative Recommendation for Industrial Live-Streaming Advertising</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Dynamic codes address live content, multiscale history captures intent, and intermittent online optimization addresses reward-policy drift. One component cannot cover all three.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Product changes, immediate user intent, and bidding value affect different paths.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24034">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.24034-tagr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-566653d184f1fc06">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tagr" data-paper-title="TAGR: Temporally Adaptive Generative Recommendation for Industrial Live-Streaming Advertising" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-2515cfaf4e666dc8">Why separate live adaptation into code allocation, interest timescales, and intermittent policy updates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atagr">TAGR: Temporally Adaptive Generative Recommendation for Industrial Live-Streaming Advertising</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Item content, users, and policies drift differently. LSID refreshes assignments behind a stable vocabulary, IAG fuses temporal interests, and IOPO runs NTP between on-policy bursts. Bounded local gates are not an online GRPO loop.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A changed product, shifted intent, and stale policy need separate fixes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24034">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.24034-tagr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2515cfaf4e666dc8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tagr" data-paper-title="TAGR: Temporally Adaptive Generative Recommendation for Industrial Live-Streaming Advertising" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-6930136a3fbe6260">Is stable LSID vocabulary the same as freezing item-to-code assignments?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atagr">TAGR: Temporally Adaptive Generative Recommendation for Industrial Live-Streaming Advertising</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Token symbols can stay stable while assignments refresh. Freezing mappings also preserves path identities. Compatibility depends on which changes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The same digits can encode a stream on a new path.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24034">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.24034-tagr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6930136a3fbe6260">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tagr" data-paper-title="TAGR: Temporally Adaptive Generative Recommendation for Industrial Live-Streaming Advertising" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d67eba5f33c53c0b">Does local TAGR run real GRPO bursts and intermittent NTP?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atagr">TAGR: Temporally Adaptive Generative Recommendation for Industrial Live-Streaming Advertising</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No live bursts or production value labels; only bounded adaptation and failure cases on static public data. Real scheduling records sampling policy, both rewards, and maintenance versions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Adding static losses does not execute a timed online GRPO update.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24034">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.24034-tagr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d67eba5f33c53c0b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tgr" data-paper-title="TGR: Advancing Industrial Recommendation from Generative-Paradigm Ranking toward Unified Generation and Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-tgr-d333ba35" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-7bd5864e166f1cb2">Why combine ranking, generation, and offline reason in TGR?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atgr">TGR: Advancing Industrial Recommendation from Generative-Paradigm Ranking toward Unified Generation and Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Industry needs scalable scoring and item/list generation at controlled latency. Offline reasoning supplies inputs without costly online rollouts; distinct modules are not one attention equation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Prepare reasoning offline, then generate and rank live candidates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.00986">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.00986-tgr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7bd5864e166f1cb2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tgr" data-paper-title="TGR: Advancing Industrial Recommendation from Generative-Paradigm Ranking toward Unified Generation and Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d75ea81538d30e34">Why put scalable ranking, hierarchical SID generation, and offline reason tokens in one framework?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atgr">TGR: Advancing Industrial Recommendation from Generative-Paradigm Ranking toward Unified Generation and Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Ranking discriminates finely, SID generation spans items and pages, and offline tokens carry prepared reasoning online. Inspect generation paths, list objectives, and reasoning interfaces separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Precompute interest explanations, generate a page from them, and rank without live long reasoning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.00986">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.00986-tgr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d75ea81538d30e34">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tgr" data-paper-title="TGR: Advancing Industrial Recommendation from Generative-Paradigm Ranking toward Unified Generation and Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-29d2f0e011d8ee0d">What is the trade-off between offline reason tokens and live inference?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atgr">TGR: Advancing Industrial Recommendation from Generative-Paradigm Ranking toward Unified Generation and Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Offline reduces critical-path latency but can age and miss abrupt context changes. Live reasoning is flexible but expensive. Compare inputs and update cadence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Yesterday&#x27;s reasoning can miss today&#x27;s trending topic.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.00986">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.00986-tgr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-29d2f0e011d8ee0d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tgr" data-paper-title="TGR: Advancing Industrial Recommendation from Generative-Paradigm Ranking toward Unified Generation and Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f873bd8a2c7dea0f">Does local path confidence reproduce production CCFormer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atgr">TGR: Advancing Industrial Recommendation from Generative-Paradigm Ranking toward Unified Generation and Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The public core omits private SID catalog, checkpoints, and live generation. Align level probabilities and list scores explicitly; proxy fusion is not deployment evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A working multi-level code score is not a complete page generator or ranker.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.00986">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.00986-tgr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f873bd8a2c7dea0f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tiger" data-paper-title="Recommender Systems with Generative Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-tiger-7436853d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-602316de33d0b529">Why quantize content into multilevel Semantic IDs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atiger">Recommender Systems with Generative Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google / Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Short discrete codes share meaning and support autoregressive generation. Content and quantization quality limit generalization, and codes must map to valid items.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Similar items share early codes and differ at fine levels.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.05065">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2305.05065-tiger/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-602316de33d0b529">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tiger" data-paper-title="Recommender Systems with Generative Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-41bf45ff5bebea3c">Why share semantics via residual SID instead of random hierarchy, and still use a collision token?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atiger">Recommender Systems with Generative Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google / Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Coarse centers and residual refinement can group related items, while finite codebooks still collide. A unique suffix resolves identity. Matched random IDs isolate hierarchy from semantic hierarchy; semantic IDs need not win.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Gardening books can share a prefix and split by subject or final collision suffix.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.05065">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2305.05065-tiger/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-41bf45ff5bebea3c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tiger" data-paper-title="Recommender Systems with Generative Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1e524d9ba84a0a5f">How does a collision token differ from the semantic prefix?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atiger">Recommender Systems with Generative Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google / Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It disambiguates item identity when several items share a semantic code. An arbitrary unique suffix is not a new semantic level.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two similar videos can share three levels but require distinct final tokens.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.05065">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2305.05065-tiger/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1e524d9ba84a0a5f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tiger" data-paper-title="Recommender Systems with Generative Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-97a2c69cd47c2932">Does local TIGER rank with a score proxy or complete code probability?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atiger">Recommender Systems with Generative Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google / Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Sum token log probabilities over valid item codes, without score fusion. Match codebooks/collisions in training and decoding; exclude invalid paths.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Omitting a level changes the complete item&#x27;s generation probability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.05065">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2305.05065-tiger/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-97a2c69cd47c2932">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tsgr" data-paper-title="TSGR: Taobao Search Generative Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-tsgr-1abc60bc" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f23c7744979bd4a8">Why encode business value in TSGR generation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atsgr">TSGR: Taobao Search Generative Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group of Alibaba / Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Semantic-only retrieval followed by isolated pre-ranking separates retrieval from value. Global and query-conditioned codes plus joint VRM connect generation states with fine business ranking.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Among semantically similar items, include transaction fit for the current query.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.18796">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.18796-tsgr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f23c7744979bd4a8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tsgr" data-paper-title="TSGR: Taobao Search Generative Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-3a964a889b237327">Why assign global and query-conditioned value codes under one semantic prefix?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atsgr">TSGR: Taobao Search Generative Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group of Alibaba / Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Semantics groups relevance, while value differs overall and by query. Parallel codes and joint VRM combine generator state with item details without a disconnected pre-ranker. Public rating proxies are not transaction value.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A middling camera accessory may be especially valuable for macro photography.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.18796">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.18796-tsgr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3a964a889b237327">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tsgr" data-paper-title="TSGR: Taobao Search Generative Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-2d588b4c7cb0beac">Why retain global and query-conditioned value codes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atsgr">TSGR: Taobao Search Generative Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group of Alibaba / Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Global summarizes broad value; conditional code expresses value for specific demand. Global can favor head items and conditional needs reliable query statistics.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A bestseller may be worse for a specialist query than a niche product.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.18796">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.18796-tsgr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2d588b4c7cb0beac">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tsgr" data-paper-title="TSGR: Taobao Search Generative Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-eea547b26501ff8d">What leakage must local TSGR IDs and VRM avoid?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atsgr">TSGR: Taobao Search Generative Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group of Alibaba / Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use training-period value estimates and code assignments, align query conditions with item identity, and update VRM jointly under protocol. Never encode test conversion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Putting a future order amount into an item code leaks the prediction target.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.18796">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.18796-tsgr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-eea547b26501ff8d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:unique" data-paper-title="UNIQUE: A Unified Retrieval and Ranking System for Large-Scale Feed Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-unique-d194acb1" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c1131a1665add327">Why use a flat UNIQUE code instead of residual levels?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aunique">UNIQUE: A Unified Retrieval and Ranking System for Large-Scale Feed Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It avoids stagewise quantization error, using feedback towers, frequency correction, and EMA for one level alongside retrieval and ranking losses. Flat codes need not uniquely identify items.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Retrieve one semantic bucket, then rank its items.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.23718">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.23718-unique/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c1131a1665add327">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:unique" data-paper-title="UNIQUE: A Unified Retrieval and Ranking System for Large-Scale Feed Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-340940bae7589d13">Why use flat codes and forbid candidates from reading each other?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aunique">UNIQUE: A Unified Retrieval and Ranking System for Large-Scale Feed Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Flat allocation avoids error accumulation and uses feedback, frequency correction, and EMA. Shared prefixes save user encoding; item/code isolation keeps scoring independent. Joint objectives connect retrieval and ranking; monitor use and collisions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Retrieve one-level code buckets and score each candidate against the same history, not its neighbors.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.23718">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.23718-unique/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-340940bae7589d13">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:unique" data-paper-title="UNIQUE: A Unified Retrieval and Ranking System for Large-Scale Feed Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-3d728475f273bb67">How does shared-prefix-only candidate attention differ from setwise attention?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aunique">UNIQUE: A Unified Retrieval and Ranking System for Large-Scale Feed Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Candidate isolation reuses user encoding and avoids peers changing scores. Setwise attention depends on the candidate set. Unified retrieval and ranking do not require item-to-item reads.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Adding a candidate should not alter an existing candidate through peer attention.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.23718">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.23718-unique/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3d728475f273bb67">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:unique" data-paper-title="UNIQUE: A Unified Retrieval and Ranking System for Large-Scale Feed Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-10e739be835f7cb5">Do straight-through quantization and balanced code usage establish retrieval quality?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aunique">UNIQUE: A Unified Retrieval and Ranking System for Large-Scale Feed Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Straight-through preserves gradients and correction helps usage, not relevance. Three small seeds do not rebuild industrial indexes, P99, or online gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Equally sized buckets can contain uniformly irrelevant mixtures.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.23718">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.23718-unique/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-10e739be835f7cb5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:unir2" data-paper-title="Unifying Generative Recall and Multi-Objective Ranking in a Single Decoder-Only Sequence" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-unir2-b2b6f557" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-38e98a94a6926bfc">Why use generated SID traces as a ranking bridge?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aunir2">Unifying Generative Recall and Multi-Objective Ranking in a Single Decoder-Only Sequence</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou / IIE, CAS / UCAS</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The generated path contains intermediate retrieval choices, beyond a shared encoder or final ID. A heterogeneous decoder reads the trace with item features.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Rank with the semantic prefixes that led to the item.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24439">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.24439-unir2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-38e98a94a6926bfc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:unir2" data-paper-title="Unifying Generative Recall and Multi-Objective Ranking in a Single Decoder-Only Sequence" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d829ee3c55f372e7">Why let ranking read SID traces but detach shared outputs and train LoRA?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aunir2">Unifying Generative Recall and Multi-Objective Ranking in a Single Decoder-Only Sequence</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou / IIE, CAS / UCAS</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Paths supply retrieval evidence. Role-specific masks share forward information, while detached shared outputs and low-rank updates reduce backward interference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Rank using outdoor→camping→tent while adjusting only ranking LoRA for new scoring preferences.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24439">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.24439-unir2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d829ee3c55f372e7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:unir2" data-paper-title="Unifying Generative Recall and Multi-Objective Ranking in a Single Decoder-Only Sequence" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-801509b74030f2f3">Why do generation and ranking queries need different masks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aunir2">Unifying Generative Recall and Multi-Objective Ranking in a Single Decoder-Only Sequence</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou / IIE, CAS / UCAS</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Generation reads only earlier SIDs; ranking can read the full path and synchronized item tokens. Future code access would leak generation targets, while restricting ranking can hide useful evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Level-two generation cannot read level three, but ranking can.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24439">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.24439-unir2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-801509b74030f2f3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:unir2" data-paper-title="Unifying Generative Recall and Multi-Objective Ranking in a Single Decoder-Only Sequence" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-9a0ab5f3e0db431b">How does ranking LoRA protect the shared generation trunk?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aunir2">Unifying Generative Recall and Multi-Objective Ranking in a Single Decoder-Only Sequence</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou / IIE, CAS / UCAS</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Stop gradients through shared Q/K/V outputs in the ranking branch and train ranking-specific LoRA. This is not freezing everything or fully sharing gradients. Local scope excludes production beams and parallelism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Ranking loss changes LoRA without updating shared generation projections through that route.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24439">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.24439-unir2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9a0ab5f3e0db431b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:unirec-coa" data-paper-title="UniRec: Bridging the Expressive Gap between Generative and Discriminative Recommendation via Chain-of-Attribute" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-unirec-coa-7ee11184" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0d1560da99d7ac98">Why generate an attribute chain before SIDs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aunirec-coa">UniRec: Bridging the Expressive Gap between Generative and Discriminative Recommendation via Chain-of-Attribute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Authors did not disclose affiliation / large-scale e-commerce platform</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Explicit category, seller, and brand context can bridge generative and discriminative representations. The chain guides content and does not establish independent language reasoning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Generate category and brand before the detailed semantic path.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.12234">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2604.12234-unirec-coa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0d1560da99d7ac98">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:unirec-coa" data-paper-title="UniRec: Bridging the Expressive Gap between Generative and Discriminative Recommendation via Chain-of-Attribute" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-5ec2902153dfbf8c">Why generate attributes before SID and constrain quantization capacity?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aunirec-coa">UniRec: Bridging the Expressive Gap between Generative and Discriminative Recommendation via Chain-of-Attribute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Authors did not disclose affiliation / large-scale e-commerce platform</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Category, seller, and brand condition generation explicitly. Capacity prevents popular codes monopolizing the space; task context handles differing needs. Early attribute errors propagate, so interpretable steps do not guarantee correct items.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Choosing dress shoes instead of sneakers early can derail the path despite precise later decoding.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.12234">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2604.12234-unirec-coa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5ec2902153dfbf8c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:unirec-coa" data-paper-title="UniRec: Bridging the Expressive Gap between Generative and Discriminative Recommendation via Chain-of-Attribute" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1ca55275b4b52784">How does capacity-limited quantization differ from maximizing popular-code likelihood?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aunirec-coa">UniRec: Bridging the Expressive Gap between Generative and Discriminative Recommendation via Chain-of-Attribute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Authors did not disclose affiliation / large-scale e-commerce platform</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Capacity limits reduce hotspots and disperse usage, while likelihood alone follows frequency. Evaluate relevance and balance together.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Avoid crowding a bucket without randomly distributing items just to equalize counts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.12234">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2604.12234-unirec-coa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1ca55275b4b52784">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:unirec-coa" data-paper-title="UniRec: Bridging the Expressive Gap between Generative and Discriminative Recommendation via Chain-of-Attribute" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-9e5f5e882d487833">Can future target behavior reveal attributes used as inputs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aunirec-coa">UniRec: Bridging the Expressive Gap between Generative and Discriminative Recommendation via Chain-of-Attribute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Authors did not disclose affiliation / large-scale e-commerce platform</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Attributes come from allowed item metadata. Target attributes can supervise generation, not be given as known answers. Public MovieLens lacks private multi-scenario serving.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Supplying the true next item&#x27;s brand leaks a clue.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.12234">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2604.12234-unirec-coa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9e5f5e882d487833">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:unisgr-v2" data-paper-title="UniSGR-V2: Stepwise Target-Side Feature Anticipation and Crossing for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-unisgr-v2-08304e35" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-8a5a68bc5d810a6a">Why predict side features for an item not generated yet?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aunisgr-v2">UniSGR-V2: Stepwise Target-Side Feature Anticipation and Crossing for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International Digital Commerce Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Item identity is unknown mid-decode. Predict continuous features by level and cross them with generation/ranking; auxiliary tasks prevent target collapse.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Estimate likely attributes before emitting a brand-related code.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.16132">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.16132-unisgr-v2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8a5a68bc5d810a6a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:unisgr-v2" data-paper-title="UniSGR-V2: Stepwise Target-Side Feature Anticipation and Crossing for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-0d266de6aee71fa6">Why predict target side information but mask semantic-to-prediction reads?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aunisgr-v2">UniSGR-V2: Stepwise Target-Side Feature Anticipation and Crossing for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International Digital Commerce Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Target features are unavailable before decoding and estimates help each level. Prevent noisy estimates from propagating into earlier semantic states, but retain output conditioning. Ranking supervision anchors targets. Full training is not reproduced locally.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Price/style estimates can guide output while staying out of prior semantic attention.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.16132">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.16132-unisgr-v2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0d266de6aee71fa6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:unisgr-v2" data-paper-title="UniSGR-V2: Stepwise Target-Side Feature Anticipation and Crossing for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-7be92ca500e528ac">How does a one-way mask differ from disabling predicted features?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aunisgr-v2">UniSGR-V2: Stepwise Target-Side Feature Anticipation and Crossing for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International Digital Commerce Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Semantic tokens cannot attend to predicted tokens; prediction can read prior semantics, and output conditioning still uses predicted features. Disabling removes the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Prevent hidden noise feedback without withholding estimated features from generation heads.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.16132">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.16132-unisgr-v2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7be92ca500e528ac">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:unisgr-v2" data-paper-title="UniSGR-V2: Stepwise Target-Side Feature Anticipation and Crossing for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-632cf77864f1705d">Why not replace the real auxiliary attribute tower with self-predictions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aunisgr-v2">UniSGR-V2: Stepwise Target-Side Feature Anticipation and Crossing for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International Digital Commerce Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A learnable target needs business labels; mutual prediction can collapse. Isolate future labels and use type-specific masks so semantic states cannot read true future attributes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two networks can agree on a constant without learning attributes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.16132">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.16132-unisgr-v2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-632cf77864f1705d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:univa" data-paper-title="Unified Value Alignment for Generative Recommendation in Industrial Advertising" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-univa-ad679aba" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0de51f7643d33b41">Does the final commercial SID level just refine item semantics?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Auniva">Unified Value Alignment for Generative Recommendation in Industrial Advertising</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent / WeChat Channels</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It keeps two semantic levels and adds commercial attributes plus within-class bid bins. Interpret the commercial mapping rather than ordinary content clusters; proxy bids are not revenue.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Similar ads can differ at the final level because of bid tier.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.05803">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.05803-univa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0de51f7643d33b41">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:univa" data-paper-title="Unified Value Alignment for Generative Recommendation in Industrial Advertising" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-9b382078c2f77bfb">Why combine commercial SID, value logits, and request-specific tries?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Auniva">Unified Value Alignment for Generative Recommendation in Industrial Advertising</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent / WeChat Channels</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Commercial IDs carry value features; fused logits and eCPM reward shape policy. The trie separately enforces current eligibility. High value does not mean legal or relevant; local value is a proxy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Block a high-bid but unavailable ad and score legal alternatives by both relevance and value.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.05803">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.05803-univa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9b382078c2f77bfb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:univa" data-paper-title="Unified Value Alignment for Generative Recommendation in Industrial Advertising" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-99696aa492087453">How does Generation-as-Ranking differ from independent post-generation ranking?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Auniva">Unified Value Alignment for Generative Recommendation in Industrial Advertising</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent / WeChat Channels</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Generation and value logits sum before normalization, so value changes every path probability. Post-ranking only reorders retrieved candidates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A high-value path can enter the beam earlier rather than be considered after recall.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.05803">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.05803-univa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-99696aa492087453">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:univa" data-paper-title="Unified Value Alignment for Generative Recommendation in Industrial Advertising" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-dbef2e81a2695f80">How distinguish local UniVA from real eCPM and personalized serving tries?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Auniva">Unified Value Alignment for Generative Recommendation in Industrial Advertising</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent / WeChat Channels</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Local network/RL/trie paths use deterministic bid/business proxies. Limit requests to currently eligible inventory and accumulate fused log probability; a globally valid ad may be illegal here.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Mask an ad not eligible in the current region.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.05803">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.05803-univa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dbef2e81a2695f80">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:wegr" data-paper-title="WeGR: Unified Generative Retrieval for Industrial Search Systems in WeChat" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-wegr-8c03ebb0" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-349baee34dd5d03a">Why grow WeGR preference optimization from short SID prefixes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Awegr">WeGR: Unified Generative Retrieval for Industrial Search Systems in WeChat</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · WeChat E-commerce Search team（正文未单列作者机构）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Full paths yield sparse reward; coarse prefixes provide early signal. Align rewarded horizon with optimized tokens to avoid updating unevaluated suffixes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Learn broad category before requiring an exact item code.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.16979">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.16979-wegr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-349baee34dd5d03a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:wegr" data-paper-title="WeGR: Unified Generative Retrieval for Industrial Search Systems in WeChat" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-560f97a3aa5441bb">Why expand both DHPO reward matching and policy gradients gradually?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Awegr">WeGR: Unified Generative Retrieval for Industrial Search Systems in WeChat</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · WeChat E-commerce Search team（正文未单列作者机构）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Short matches densify initially sparse rewards and restrict updates to evaluated tokens. Expand to full codes over time. Multi-positive SFT and CoCo-VAE serve separate roles; local evidence is bounded.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reward outdoor first, then camping, then the full tent path without reinforcing wrong unevaluated suffixes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.16979">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.16979-wegr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-560f97a3aa5441bb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:wegr" data-paper-title="WeGR: Unified Generative Retrieval for Industrial Search Systems in WeChat" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-985a686fe1d1692f">How does CoCo-VAE collision loss differ from entropy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Awegr">WeGR: Unified Generative Retrieval for Industrial Search Systems in WeChat</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · WeChat E-commerce Search team（正文未单列作者机构）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Collision measures overlap across examples; entropy measures one distribution&#x27;s spread. Uniform distributions can have high entropy and completely overlap.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Assigning every item uniformly across all codes is not discriminative.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.16979">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.16979-wegr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-985a686fe1d1692f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:wegr" data-paper-title="WeGR: Unified Generative Retrieval for Industrial Search Systems in WeChat" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d623e744cb8952fe">Does WeGR refresh low-utilization codes at every layer?</h2>
