<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Awegr">WeGR: Unified Generative Retrieval for Industrial Search Systems in WeChat</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · WeChat E-commerce Search team（正文未单列作者机构）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Refresh from first-layer hit EMA only. Keep deeper layers fixed for refresh, align DHPO prefix length to schedule, and add multisession-positive NLL per session. Full-sequence loss is not progressive horizon.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>At h=1, later codes must not receive full gradients from the prefix reward.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.16979">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.16979-wegr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d623e744cb8952fe">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:xrec" data-paper-title="X-Rec Technical Report" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-xrec-d9eceda3" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-9284c7fba5ba0f2c">Why generate X-Rec triggers on the item embedding sphere?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Axrec">X-Rec Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · TikTok (ByteDance)</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Normalized continuous vectors query multiple regions directly without SID quantization or token-by-token decoding. Anchors condition flow toward valid item neighborhoods.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Generate different interest directions and retrieve nearby catalog items.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.29180">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.29180-xrec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9284c7fba5ba0f2c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:xrec" data-paper-title="X-Rec Technical Report" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-4756ebc069854072">Why condition flow on normalized item space instead of generating SID tokens?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Axrec">X-Rec Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · TikTok (ByteDance)</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Continuous triggers avoid code quantization and use ANN directly. Coarse anchors condition geodesic noise-to-item flow; tangent projection preserves geometry. Cache earlier history layers and denoise final-layer tokens. Multistep cost remains and local low-budget outcomes are negative.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Generate camera/lens directions around a photography anchor rather than decoding integer IDs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.29180">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.29180-xrec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4756ebc069854072">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:xrec" data-paper-title="X-Rec Technical Report" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a33bd2600d866b14">How does spherical flow differ from Euclidean interpolation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Axrec">X-Rec Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · TikTok (ByteDance)</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Geodesic paths and tangent projection preserve normalization. Straight lines can leave the sphere. Reusing earlier history layers is a separate efficiency design.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The midpoint of two unit vectors is generally not unit length.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:xrec" data-paper-title="X-Rec Technical Report" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">

<h2 id="qa-834265e483da0699">Does local X-Rec have a GPU throughput receipt, and what runs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Axrec">X-Rec Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · TikTok (ByteDance)</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. CPU runs scaled anchors, geodesic RFM, final-layer KV reuse, and spherical Euler. No industrial ANN, streaming, or online A/B; CPU timings are not production throughput.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Caching history verifies skipped computation without proving A100 gains.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pailitao-mmsearch2" data-paper-title="PailitaoMMSearch2.0 Technical Report: Scaling Generative Retrieval to Unified End-to-End Multimodal Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-pailitao-mmsearch2-204499bd" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-6ad4ec1f2700540d">Does PailitaoMMSearch2.0 rewrite queries or directly generate items?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apailitao-mmsearch2">PailitaoMMSearch2.0 Technical Report: Scaling Generative Retrieval to Unified End-to-End Multimodal Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-29 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group of Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It consumes the original image and free text and generates three-level SIDs that map to products. Decoding produces candidates. Some deployments still mix them with incumbent retrieval results; end-to-end generation does not remove every production module.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Upload a shirt and request matching pants; outputs are product IDs, not just a rewritten query for another engine.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式, 论文离线与线上效果. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pailitao-mmsearch2" data-paper-title="PailitaoMMSearch2.0 Technical Report: Scaling Generative Retrieval to Unified End-to-End Multimodal Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8032636210dd476d">Why does Sample–Beam separate sampled reasoning from item beam generation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apailitao-mmsearch2">PailitaoMMSearch2.0 Technical Report: Scaling Generative Retrieval to Unified End-to-End Multimodal Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-29 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group of Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Serving returns an item set; sampling one response does not match that structure. Sample reasoning, then beam-expand the SID to train RL on a serving-like candidate set. Intent rewards and trajectories are still needed; beam search alone is not the full method.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Expand ten product codes under one rationale instead of sampling ten unrelated rationale–ID pairs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36958v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../recommendation-components/2610.36958-pailitao-mmsearch2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8032636210dd476d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pailitao-mmsearch2" data-paper-title="PailitaoMMSearch2.0 Technical Report: Scaling Generative Retrieval to Unified End-to-End Multimodal Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">

<h2 id="qa-ba1eaa41311ff0a8">Does more reasoning always improve PailitaoMMSearch2.0 retrieval?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apailitao-mmsearch2">PailitaoMMSearch2.0 Technical Report: Scaling Generative Retrieval to Unified End-to-End Multimodal Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-29 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group of Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The 0.8B No-think variant has highest macro ER; 2B Low-think better balances overall quality and latency, and 4B varies by intent. Consider scale, intent and serving cost rather than generalizing a single optimum.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A clearly visible exact-match attribute may need no rationale, while a match with several constraints can benefit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 论文离线与线上效果. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<h2 id="qa-191febc5125e9909">Can a 0.58 percentage-point CTR gain be reported as 0.58% relative?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apailitao-mmsearch2">PailitaoMMSearch2.0 Technical Report: Scaling Generative Retrieval to Unified End-to-End Multimodal Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-29 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group of Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Percentage points are absolute; relative change depends on baseline CTR. The paper&#x27;s result is from full deployment. This repository records the work only, without model, private-data training or A/B; don&#x27;t attribute production lift to a local stub.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: 10%→10.58% is +0.58 points but +5.8% relative. This illustrates units, not the paper baseline.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 论文离线与线上效果, 本地复现与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pinger" data-paper-title="PinGER: Token-Efficient Generative Retrieval with Semantic IDs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-pinger-bbbb9458" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f9327d3b5e34e40b">Why keep SIDs during PinGER training but remove historical SIDs at serving?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apinger">PinGER: Token-Efficient Generative Retrieval with Semantic IDs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-30 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Asymmetric masking sends historical item information forward only through dense tokens. Historical SID positions are not read by other items or dense states, so removing those positions does not alter retained dense states. Dense input can still incorporate SID features.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A historical item occupies three SID positions and one dense position during training. Keeping only the dense position can preserve its attention output if inputs match.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.33435v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../recommendation-components/2610.33435-pinger/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f9327d3b5e34e40b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pinger" data-paper-title="PinGER: Token-Efficient Generative Retrieval with Semantic IDs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-29956241de9aa37e">Why isn&#x27;t prefix diversity just subtracting a constant for duplicate next tokens?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apinger">PinGER: Token-Efficient Generative Retrieval with Semantic IDs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-30 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Penalty depends on longest common prefix depth between parent beams and accumulated chosen slots, including the same parent. Deeper shared prefixes penalize repeated subtrees more. The next token alone drops hierarchy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Parents (1,2) and (1,3) share depth one; (1,2) with itself shares depth two. After picking its child, penalties differ.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.33435v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../recommendation-components/2610.33435-pinger/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-29956241de9aa37e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pinger" data-paper-title="PinGER: Token-Efficient Generative Retrieval with Semantic IDs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-0ae0c3df86c6a36e">Does improved online interest coverage guarantee higher offline recall?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apinger">PinGER: Token-Efficient Generative Retrieval with Semantic IDs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-30 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Increasing lambda from 0 to 3 increases distinct@1 but lowers R@100 in the paper. A stronger online penalty can still suit its objectives/settings. Do not conflate offline tables with production A/B under a different beam width.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: 100 items from one category may hit an established preference but miss other interests. Diversity trades metrics off.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 论文离线与线上效果. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.33435v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../recommendation-components/2610.33435-pinger/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0ae0c3df86c6a36e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pinger" data-paper-title="PinGER: Token-Efficient Generative Retrieval with Semantic IDs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a40d6e62f3c4f3a9">Why does PinGER DPO accumulate every prefix and retain an NTP anchor?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apinger">PinGER: Token-Efficient Generative Retrieval with Semantic IDs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-30 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Per-level loss gives earlier SID decisions preference signal; using only full IDs changes the objective. NTP limits drift. Reference margin offsets the logistic input, not a hard stop-gradient for correct ranking. Local checks are formula-only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: For three levels sum losses for prefixes 1, 1–2 and 1–3, then add NTP. Tripling only the final loss differs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.33435v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../recommendation-components/2610.33435-pinger/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a40d6e62f3c4f3a9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>

<details class="ar-learning-guide" markdown="1"><summary>Topic guide and reading order</summary>

## Start with this question

What changes when items are represented as tokens?

## Takeaway

Generative retrieval predicts item codes conditioned on the user. Create catalog-recoverable identifiers, learn the code sequence distribution, and constrain decoding to eligible items. TIGER connects quantization to autoregressive retrieval, COBRA cascades sparse codes and dense representations, and PLUM continues pretraining an existing LM on recommendation data. Preference optimization and reasoning tokens change training or search. PinGER retains SID labels at every level during training but masks later history to read only dense tokens, so prior SIDs can be removed at serving. Input cost, prefix coverage, and catalog validity are different contracts.

## Example

Suppose the catalog contains codes (3,7) and (3,9), but the model gives (3,5) high probability. A plausible-looking code is not an eligible item. Constrain decoding to the catalog and handle collisions or retain a later disambiguation path.

## Common pitfall

Lower token loss need not raise Recall. Wider beams cannot recover items excluded by a bad codebook or prefix constraint. Some papers generate whole lists; classify by the main generation mechanism and see reranking for slate value. Scaled local training is not production-scale reproduction.

## Reading order

Read TIGER for discrete ID generation, COBRA for sparse–dense cascades, and PLUM for continued pretraining of an existing LM. All have local core pipelines, but TIGER and PLUM did not verify final local retrieval gains.

1. [Recommender Systems with Generative Retrieval](../../../../reproductions/2305.05065-tiger/README-en.md) · [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.05065)
2. [Sparse Meets Dense: Unified Generative Recommendations with Cascaded Sparse-Dense Representations](../../../../reproductions/2503.02453-cobra/README-en.md) · [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.02453)
3. [PLUM: Adapting Pre-trained Language Models for Industrial-scale Generative Recommendations](../../../../reproductions/2510.07784-plum/README-en.md) · [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.07784)

## Check your understanding

Why can a correctly formatted three-level SID still fail retrieval?

??? note "Show suggested answer"

    Format guarantees length and vocabulary membership only. The combination can be absent, ambiguous, or irrelevant. Check catalog reachability, collision handling, coverage, and ranking on an isolated test set.

</details>
